t: WPC Smart Messages for WooCommerce before 4.3.6 Information Disclosure via Shortcodes
d: WPC Smart Messages for WooCommerce plugin before 4.3.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor or Author privileges to disclose arbitrary post meta and private product data by supplying attacker-controlled id and key attributes to the [wpcsm_product_field] and [wpcsm_product_data] shortcodes without any capability or protected-meta checks. Attackers can embed these shortcodes in a published post to exfiltrate sensitive order data such as billing email, phone, and address stored as post meta, as well as private or draft product descriptions and purchase notes, exposing confidential customer and business information to unauthenticated site visitors.

t: continuedev continue Dev Data Logging log.ts DataLogger.logDevData information disclosure
d: A flaw has been found in continuedev continue up to 2.1.0. This affects the function DataLogger.logDevData of the file core/data/log.ts of the component Dev Data Logging. This manipulation causes information disclosure. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: continuedev continue Docs Crawler DocsCrawler.ts DocsCrawler server-side request forgery
d: A vulnerability was detected in continuedev continue 2.0.0/2.1.0. Affected by this issue is the function DocsCrawler of the file core/indexing/docs/crawlers/DocsCrawler.ts of the component Docs Crawler. The manipulation of the argument startUrl/useLocalCrawling results in server-side request forgery. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The attack requires a high level of complexity. The exploitation is known to be difficult. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: LibreChat: Cross-User Message Injection via Parameter Confusion
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, POST /api/messages/:conversationId authorizes req.params.conversationId in api/server/middleware/validateMessageReq.js but persists attacker-controlled req.body.conversationId through api/server/routes/messages.js. An authenticated attacker can use an owned conversation in the URL while naming a victim conversation in the body, causing an attacker-controlled message to be stored in the victim conversation. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

t: continuedev continue Mermaid Diagram Renderer ContinueGUIWebviewViewProvider.ts getSidebarContent os command injection
d: A security vulnerability has been detected in continuedev continue 2.0.0/2.1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is the function getSidebarContent of the file extensions/vscode/src/ContinueGUIWebviewViewProvider.ts of the component Mermaid Diagram Renderer. The manipulation leads to os command injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: LibreChat: Server-Side ReDoS via Unescaped Regex in Principal Search
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.9, GET /api/permissions/search-principals passes the q parameter to JavaScript RegExp construction and MongoDB regex queries in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/userGroup.ts findGroupsByNamePattern and searchPrincipals without escaping metacharacters. An authenticated user with people-picker permission can submit a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that blocks the Node.js event loop and makes the service unresponsive to concurrent users; invalid patterns can also produce server errors. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.9.

t: LibreChat: MCP OAuth requests can follow redirects to internal URLs after SSRF validation
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.8, packages/api/src/mcp/oauth/handler.ts createOAuthFetch validates only the initial destination for MCP OAuth discovery, registration, token, refresh, and revocation requests, then uses redirect-following fetch behavior without validating each redirect target. An attacker who can initiate MCP OAuth against a controlled endpoint can redirect server requests to internal or private addresses, reaching services that the initial SSRF checks should block. The separate MCP transport path already validates redirects and is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.8.

t: LibreChat: Shared-Agent Editor Can Exfiltrate Owner Action API Keys via OpenAPI Spec Swap
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/agents/actions/:agent_id in api/server/routes/agents/actions.js loads an existing action with owner credentials and merges editor-controlled metadata.domain and metadata.raw_spec while preserving metadata.api_key and related OAuth client secrets. A collaborator with EDIT permission can repoint an action to an attacker-controlled host, and a later tool invocation decrypts and sends the retained owner credential to that destination. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

t: LibreChat: Unauthenticated User Enumeration via Email Verification Endpoint
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, unauthenticated POST /api/user/verify requests in api/server/routes/user.js call api/server/services/AuthService.js verifyEmail and return distinct responses for unknown, verified, and unverified email addresses and the route lacks request throttling. A remote attacker can submit candidate addresses with invalid tokens to enumerate registered accounts and verification state, supporting targeted phishing or credential attacks. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

t: LibreChat: Password Reset Can Wipe Email-Verification Tokens When Verification Is Enforced
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/requestPasswordReset calls deleteTokens by user ID before creating a reset token, while password-reset and email-verification records in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/token.ts have no populated flow type. When password reset is enabled and email verification is enforced, an unauthenticated attacker who knows a target email can repeatedly delete pending verification tokens and prevent account verification until the unverified account expires. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

t: LibreChat: Missing Rate Limiting on 2FA Verification Endpoint Allows TOTP Guessing Attempts
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/2fa/verify-temp in api/server/routes/auth.js calls verify2FAWithTempToken and accepts repeated TOTP or backup-code guesses without a dedicated attempt limiter. An attacker must first possess valid primary credentials and a valid five-minute temp token, but can then make repeated second-factor attempts and obtain a full session if a valid code is guessed. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

t: LibreChat: Federated OAuth Tokens Exposed via `/api/user` Endpoint
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.8.5 until 0.8.6, GET /api/user in api/server/controllers/UserController.js getUserController serializes federatedTokens and tokenset to the authenticated browser because an earlier response-sanitization fix was not applied to this endpoint. Browser-context script can obtain OAuth access, ID, and refresh credentials that were intended to remain server-side. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

t: LibreChat: Unauthorized File Content Access via Chat Attachment file_id
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, packages/data-schemas/src/methods/file.ts updateFileUsage accepts chat attachment files[].file_id values without restricting the lookup to the authenticated owner. An authenticated attacker who obtains another user's file identifier, including through GET /api/share/{shareId} for a shared conversation, can attach that file to a chat, causing extracted document text to enter the model context. The same operation can remove expiration metadata from the victim file. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

t: LibreChat: Remote MCP Server Description XSS via Unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML; secondary Admin Banner sink lacks DOMPurify
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, client/src/components/Chat/Input/MCPConfigDialog.tsx renders the remote MCP details.description value through dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing a malicious MCP server to execute script when a user opens the configuration dialog. The secondary client/src/components/Banners/Banner.tsx sink similarly renders administrator-controlled banner.message HTML without sanitization for all users. Script execution occurs in the LibreChat browser origin and can expose browser-context data or alter displayed content. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

t: LibreChat: Pre-registration account takeover via attacker-controlled `provider` field and social-login email fallback
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.7.0 until 0.8.6, when local registration is enabled and at least one social provider is configured, POST /api/auth/register passes an unparsed request object into api/server/services/AuthService.js, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist a forged provider value for a known victim email. The api/strategies/socialLogin.js email-fallback path then accepts the planted record when the victim signs in because it compares the stored provider name without requiring the provider subject identifier. The victim OAuth session and the attacker local-password session become bound to the same user record, giving the attacker persistent read and write access to data created by the victim. The first-user administrator role is an additional conditional impact only on a fresh deployment. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

t: LibreChat: Plaintext password logged on login validation error
d: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, the POST /api/auth/login local-login validation path in api/strategies/localStrategy.js logs req.body, including the submitted plaintext password, during a Zod validation failure. The standard browser form validation makes this path less likely through the normal interface, but a direct invalid login request can reach it, and the logging formatter does not redact the password stored in metadata. A principal with access to application stdout, error logs, or journal output can recover the submitted credential. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

t: continuedev continue Edit Tool editImpl.ts validateSearchAndReplaceFilepath path traversal
d: A weakness has been identified in continuedev continue 2.0.0/2.1.0. Affected is the function validateSearchAndReplaceFilepath of the file gui/src/util/clientTools/editImpl.ts of the component Edit Tool. Executing a manipulation can lead to path traversal. The attack requires local access. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: codebase-memory-mcp: Catastrophic backtracking in .gitignore glob matching lets a repository stall the indexer
d: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.10.0, the indexer's .gitignore matcher implemented * and ** through recursive backtracking without a work bound. A repository containing a pattern with repeated wildcard groups and a long path could make matching work grow exponentially, allowing a single ignore rule to stall discovery indefinitely and, before worker isolation, stall the server. The impact is limited to availability, and the bounded matcher does not claim that every expensive input is eliminated. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.

t: codebase-memory-mcp: Heap buffer overflow on artifact import via int-truncated decompression capacity
d: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

t: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program authentication mechanism bypass through client-controlled flow selection
d: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program allows attackers with valid local application credentials to establish an application session by sending JSON POST requests to the application's login endpoint without a Referrer header or completing the intended Keycloak flow. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

t: codebase-memory-mcp: Stack out-of-bounds write in query_graph via a RETURN or WITH clause with more than 32 items
d: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, the Cypher parser accepted an unbounded number of projection items in RETURN and WITH clauses while projection executors indexed fixed 32-element stack arrays using the parsed count. A query_graph query with more than 32 projection items could therefore write beyond those arrays, and a related result-column path could read uninitialized stack slots even when no node matched. Any caller of query_graph, including an agent whose query is influenced by untrusted content, could cause a reliable server crash and potentially compromise process confidentiality and integrity. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

t: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program unsalted MD5 hash for password storage
d: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program stores local user passwords as unsalted MD5 hashes. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

t: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program unauthenticated user creation
d: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program contains a vulnerable endpoint that allows an unauthenticated attacker, without a cookie header, to send a POST request resulting in the creation of a new user. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

t: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program unauthenticated user deletion
d: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program accepts a POST request from an unauthenticated user, with no cookie header, to a specific endpoint allowing for the deletion of specified users. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

t: codebase-memory-mcp: git option injection through base_branch in detect_changes allows writing a file outside the project
d: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, the detect_changes tool validated the base_branch argument for shell metacharacters but omitted the leading-dash check before placing the value in the revision position of a git diff command. Git therefore interpreted an option-shaped base_branch value, including --output, as a command option instead of a revision, allowing a caller to create or overwrite a caller-chosen file with Git diff output under the server process's permissions. Arbitrary code execution was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

t: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program unauthenticated SQL Injection
d: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program allows an unauthenticated user to inject unauthorized SQL commands that allow the attacker to gain root access and complete control over the database. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

t: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program unauthenticated user enumeration
d: U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to access a vulnerable endpoint that returns a list of application users and their permissions in plaintext. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

t: codebase-memory-mcp: UI process-kill route skipped the ownership check on Windows, allowing termination of arbitrary processes
d: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.1-rc.1, the optional graph UI's POST /api/process-kill route omitted the indexing-job ownership check on Windows while retaining that check on POSIX systems. A requester able to reach the optional UI could supply an arbitrary process identifier, causing TerminateProcess to stop any process that the server user was permitted to terminate. The flaw affects the Windows-specific process termination path and can cause a high availability impact without disclosing or modifying data. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.1-rc.1.

t: MaxKB: Eval Injection via Custom Tool "Init Param" Validator Rule Allows Arbitrary JavaScript Execution
d: MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.

t: Open Robotics RViz fillIndexBuffer Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
d: Open Robotics RViz fillIndexBuffer Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Open Robotics RViz. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of mesh resources in PointCloud and Marker displays. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-32652.

t: Open Robotics ROS 2 sros2 load_policy XML External Entity Processing Information Disclosure Vulnerability
d: Open Robotics ROS 2 sros2 load_policy XML External Entity Processing Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Open Robotics ROS 2. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file. The specific flaw exists within the parsing of policy XML files. Due to the improper restriction of XML External Entity (XXE) references, a crafted document specifying a URI causes the XML parser to access the URI and embed the contents back into the XML document for further processing. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current user. Was ZDI-CAN-32121.

t: RabbitMQ: AMQP 1.0 post-body properties bypass user-ID validation and reach consumers
d: RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. In the affected revision identified by the advisory, the AMQP 1.0 server_mode parser in deps/amqp10_common/src/amqp10_binary_parser.erl stops at the first body section and preserves the remaining bytes in bare_and_footer without validating message-section order. An authenticated publisher with write permission can place a properties section carrying a forged user-id after the body, causing rabbit_access_control:check_user_id/2 to see no user-id while permissive downstream AMQP 1.0 decoders or AMQP 0-9-1 conversion through classic and quorum queues expose the forged identity. Applications that rely on RabbitMQ-validated user-id metadata can therefore accept attacker-controlled publisher attribution. Strict consumers that reject out-of-order sections are not vulnerable to identity spoofing, and the issue does not bypass broker routing or destination authorization. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.5.

t: Soar Cloud System Human Resources client.aspx cross site scripting
d: A vulnerability was determined in Soar Cloud System Human Resources up to 7.3.2026.0112. This impacts an unknown function of the file /client.aspx. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. t: G DATA Total Security TSNxGService Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
d: G DATA Total Security TSNxGService Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the TSNxGService service. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to delete a file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28663.

The service restores archives from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28666.

t: D-Link DCS-935L Local Recording CGI setconf.cgi loginRouter os command injection
d: A vulnerability was found in D-Link DCS-935L 1.10.01. This affects the function loginRouter of the file web/cgi-bin/localrecording/setconf.cgi of the component Local Recording CGI. Performing a manipulation of the argument account/password results in os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

t: pip bundles compromised eMudhra certificates via certifi
d: pip prior to v26.2.2 the certifi bundled with pip contains the compromised eMudhra certificates. Upgrading to a secure version of pip should be done either by first upgrading Python to a version that rejects the compromised intermediates (CVE-2026-115557) or use hash pinning with a known-secure version of pip. pip is not vulnerable when using a Python version that rejects the compromised certificates. See the references below for more information.

t: MapServer: PostgreSQL JOIN second-order SQL injection in src/mappostgresql.c
d: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

t: MapServer: Reflected XSS in WMS OpenLayers output via the `X-Forwarded-Host` header
d: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

t: MapServer: Heap buffer overflow in WMS GetLegendGraphic via repeated LAYER parameters
d: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 8.2.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated attacker can send a WMS GetLegendGraphic request with a nonempty BBOX and repeated LAYER parameters to trigger a heap buffer overflow in msWMSDispatch() in src/mapwms.cpp. The handler appends synthesized entries to cgiRequestObj.ParamNames and cgiRequestObj.ParamValues at NumParams without retaining the arrays' capacity or reallocating them, while incrementing NumParams inside the loop. Once the parser's hidden capacity is exhausted, the writes pass the heap allocation boundary. A single request can corrupt heap memory and crash the process; code execution may be possible but was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

t: MapServer Reflected XSS via unescaped offset/limit query params injected into <script> in OGC API Features HTML output
d: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, an unauthenticated reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in OGC API Features collection-items HTML output allows crafted offset or limit query parameter values from raw CGI request handling in src/mapogcapi.cpp to reach template.params.offset or template.params.limit. share/ogcapi/templates/html-bootstrap/collection-items.html inserts those values without quoting or escaping into a script element. A victim who follows a crafted request can have the script element terminated by attacker-controlled markup, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute under the MapServer origin and enabling access to browser-session data, actions as the victim, and content manipulation. This issue is fixed in 8.6.5.

t: MapServer: WCS POST: NULL-Dereference Denial of Service When `BoundingBox` Omits `crs`
d: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 4.4.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a WCS GetCoverage XML POST request whose BoundingBox element omits the crs attribute, causing xmlGetProp() in src/mapwcs.cpp to return null. msWCSParseRequest() then calls string functions on the null value before normal WCS exception handling, crashing the CGI or FastCGI worker. The analogous KVP or GET path is not affected because it obtains a count-validated, non-null token. A single request can terminate one worker, and repeated requests can exhaust a fixed worker pool and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

t: MapServer: MySQL JOIN second-order SQL injection in src/mapjoin.c
d: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's MySQL JOIN implementation in src/mapjoin.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN ... FROM into joininfo->target and inserts it into the query built by msMySQLJoinNext() without parameterization or SQL escaping. When MySQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute, including through imported shapefile or DBF data or another untrusted spatial source, can inject SQL operators or expressions that change the intended JOIN predicate. This can bypass the intended key comparison and expose unrelated records from the MySQL or MariaDB JOIN table through output templates, query responses, or downstream application logic. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

t: NukeViet CMS: Stored XSS via internal marker injection in iframe srcdoc sanitization
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.08 until 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker can place NukeViet's internal {@[, ]@}, [@{, and }@] sanitizer markers in an iframe srcdoc value by encoding square brackets as HTML entities. Recursive NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() processing decodes the characters, accepts the forged marker, and later converts it to real markup without normal tag or attribute filtering. Because an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe shares the parent origin and iframe is enabled by default through NV_ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS, stored Contact messages, comments with the editor enabled, or submitted articles can execute JavaScript with the viewer's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

t: WordPress Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor plugin <= 5.1.2 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in BdThemes Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor bdthemes-prime-slider-lite allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor: from n/a through 5.1.2.

t: WordPress Element Pack Elementor Addons plugin <= 10.0.9 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability

t: WordPress Spectra plugin <= 2.20.5 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability

t: WordPress Appointment Hour Booking plugin <= 1.6.06 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability

t: WordPress AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter plugin <= 11.1.0 - Sensitive Data Exposure vulnerability
d: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in Datasolution AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter acymailing allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter: from n/a through 11.1.0.

t: WordPress Newsletters plugin <= 4.18.2 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Tribulant Software Newsletters newsletters-lite allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Newsletters: from n/a through 4.18.2.

t: WordPress WP Job Portal plugin <= 2.8.1 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Ahmad WP Job Portal wp-job-portal allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects WP Job Portal: from n/a through 2.8.1.

d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Ays Pro Quiz Maker quiz-maker allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects Quiz Maker: from n/a through 6.7.1.99.

t: WordPress OttoKit plugin <= 1.1.42 - Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability
d: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Brainstorm Force OttoKit suretriggers allows Server Side Request Forgery.This issue affects OttoKit: from n/a through 1.1.42.

t: WordPress Knit Pay plugin <= 9.6.4.0 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Knit Pay Knit Pay knit-pay allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Knit Pay: from n/a through 9.6.4.0.

t: Elecbrakes Missing Authentication for Critical Function
d: The affected products have an unauthenticated command injection, which may allow an in-range BLE device to gain access to write to the control interface and influence braking with no authentication or pairing.

t: NukeViet CMS: Stored XSS via SVG upload: the sanitizer is blind to markup hidden inside an internal DTD entity
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker with access to an SVG upload flow can hide a script element in an internal DTD entity. NukeViet\Files\Upload::check_svg_tmpfile() loads the document without entity expansion, leaving a DOMEntityReference, and sanitize_svg_dom() inspects only element nodes, while browsers expand the entity when the stored file is served as image/svg+xml. The SVG path also returned before verify_image() and preserved the original bytes, so the hidden script reached disk unchanged. Guest comment attachments make the upload unauthenticated only when a module's comment feature is open to the All or Guest group and allowattachcomm is enabled; module administrators can also use the file manager, allowing same-origin script execution in an administrator's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

t: Elecbrakes Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
d: No replay or command-integrity protection. Commands lack sequence numbers, nonces, or session tokens; captured commands can be replayed, and the last command persists across sessions.

t: NukeViet CMS: Reflected XSS in news module search via double URL decoding of the q parameter
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.

t: Elecbrakes Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
d: The affected products use an unprotected firmware-update channel, which may allow for unauthorized firmware modification.

t: NukeViet CMS: Remote Code Execution via image-upload bypass chain (PHP short-tag detection bypass + double-extension filename)
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

t: NukeViet CMS: Unauthenticated Stored XSS in the Contact module via HTML sanitizer bypass
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit Contact module content containing numeric HTML entities with more than eight leading zeros in a URL-bearing attribute. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() does not decode that form before filterAttr() checks for a javascript: scheme, but browsers decode it when rendering the stored content. With an allowed tag such as the default iframe, the reconstructed script URL executes in the administration origin when staff view the message, permitting session-riding actions while remaining unable to read the HttpOnly session cookie directly. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

t: NukeViet CMS: Unauthenticated Stored XSS in the Contact module
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 3.x release line until 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit a Contact module message containing an event-handler attribute prefixed by a slash. NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() tokenizes attributes using only ASCII spaces, so it sees /onerror and misses the ^on denylist, while the browser treats the slash as a separator and activates onerror. The message is stored and rendered without output encoding in the administration panel, which lacks a Content Security Policy, allowing same-origin JavaScript execution when an administrator opens the message. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

t: NukeViet CMS: Authenticated path traversal to arbitrary file write via S/MIME certificate CN in SMTP settings
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.6.01, an authenticated settings-module administrator can upload a PKCS#12 S/MIME certificate whose X.509 Subject CN contains path separators and traversal components. The smimeadd handler in admin/settings/smtp.php applies only an at-sign replacement before using the CN in .key, .crt, and .pem paths beneath data/certs. Traversal can select attacker-chosen paths outside data/certs, but writes remain constrained to already-existing writable directories and the permitted extensions. Within that constraint, attacker-controlled PEM data can overwrite certificate assets, including a DKIM private key; when the curl.cainfo PHP directive is empty, the attacker can also replace cacert.pem and undermine outbound TLS verification. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

t: NukeViet: Pre-authentication SSRF via incomplete X-Forwarded-Host fix
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

t: libumqtt Integer Underflow
d: libumqtt is vulnerable to an integer underflow which may allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service, memory corruption, or information disclosure.

t: NukeViet CMS: Remote Code Execution via unrestricted custom field validation callback in the `users` module
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, a super-administrator satisfying the NV_IS_SPADMIN gate can use modules/users/admin/fields.php to store an arbitrary existing PHP function in the func_callback setting for a custom profile field because the callback name is checked only with function_exists() and no allowlist restricts which function may be selected. modules/users/fields.check.php later invokes that function through call_user_func() when the field is validated through registration, profile editing, or administrator editing. Selecting a command-execution function crosses the super-administrator to operating-system boundary and executes commands as the web-server account, while ordinary users can trigger the stored callback after it is configured. Because the remediation validates callbacks only when they are written, upgrading does not remove a malicious callback already stored in the database, which must be cleaned manually. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

t: NukeVie: Login Lockout Bypass via Untrusted Forwarded-IP Headers
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can rotate X-Forwarded-For because vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Ips.php accepts forwarded client-IP headers without first confirming that REMOTE_ADDR is a trusted proxy. The resulting NV_CLIENT_IP keys the administrator login blocker in includes/core/admin_login.php; changing only the header value bypasses that lockout and permits effectively unlimited password guesses. The same spoofable address is also consumed by the user login blocker in modules/users/funcs/login.php, IP restrictions, bans, flood controls, and security logs, but those additional code-level effects were not dynamically demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

t: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in Amazon awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server
d: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the file access checks in Amazon awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server 1.0.10 through 1.0.20 might allow a context-dependent actor, via crafted document content processed by an MCP client, to read files outside the intended base directory and, in 1.0.12 through 1.0.20, to write PNG slide images outside it. This occurs when DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR is not set or is empty and the CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST environment variable is present. Versions before 1.0.10 do not restrict file access to a base directory. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.0.21 or later. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can set DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR to the directory that holds their documents. Do not set it to /, which removes the restriction.

t: NukeViet CMS: PHP Object Injection to RCE in extension store via unverified HTTP response
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.00, a network attacker who can alter outbound traffic to the extension store can exploit the HTTP client's disabled sslverify setting to substitute a serialized response. Extension-store handlers pass the response to unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction, allowing an in-tree GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget to write attacker-controlled content to a chosen path. When a GODADMIN opens or uses the store list, detail, install, or update functions, the substituted response can write a PHP file under the web root and execute code as the web-server user. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.00.

t: NukeViet CMS: Multiple Anti-XSS Filter Bypasses Leading to Stored XSS in News Module
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, a user with news-posting permission can bypass NukeViet\Core\Request::filterAttr() by prefixing an event-handler attribute with an ASCII form-feed character, which PHP trimming preserves but browsers treat as whitespace. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() omitted a decimal HTML entity tab embedded in a javascript: URI. These parser differences allow persistent event handlers or script URLs to survive filtering in vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Request.php and execute for visitors, including administrators. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

t: NukeViet CMS: Path Traversal to Arbitrary File Deletion in Edit Comment Function
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an authenticated administrator can submit a crafted attach value to modules/comment/admin/edit.php. The handler removed a fixed-length upload prefix without validating containment, allowing padding followed by a traversal path to be stored in the database. When the comment is deleted, modules/comment/admin/del.php joins the stored path to NV_UPLOADS_REAL_DIR and passes it to nv_deletefile(), whose realpath() check restricts deletion only to NV_ROOTDIR rather than the upload directory, permitting deletion of application files such as config.php and causing an outage. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

t: NukeViet CMS: Unauthenticated Reflected XSS in Comment Module
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, the Comment module accepts attacker-controlled base64 content in the status_comment parameter through modules/comment/funcs/main.php; modules/comment/comment.php decodes it with nv_base64_decode() and assigns it to STATUS_COMMENT without output escaping. The required checkss token was derived from the site-wide NV_CACHE_PREFIX rather than NV_CHECK_SESSION, so a token disclosed in public comment markup could be reused across sessions in a crafted URL. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore cause decoded HTML or JavaScript to render in a victim's browser and perform phishing or same-origin actions. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

t: NukeViet: stored XSS through comment reply display names
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 4.x release line until 4.5.09, a low-privileged authenticated user can store script-breaking content in the first_name and last_name profile fields used to form a comment display name. Both reply links in themes/default/modules/comment/comment.tpl interpolate {COMMENT.post_name} into the inline onclick call to nv_commment_feedback(). HTML numeric references produced by Request::_get_title() are decoded by the browser before JavaScript parsing, so clicking Reply can terminate the string and execute attacker-controlled JavaScript in the visitor's origin, including an administrator's session. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

t: NukeViet CMS: Pre-authentication SSRF via X-Forwarded-Host in NukeViet
d: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the __serverInfoUpdate=1 field while controlling X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto. NukeViet\Core\Server::standardizeHost() did not validate the forwarded host against my_domains, and a trailing slash could preserve an attacker-selected port that server_info_update() used to construct a cURL request in includes/ini.php before authentication. The blind, HEAD-only request uses a fixed path, but it permits internal host and port discovery and can poison cached server_headers. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

monailabel (aka MONAI Label) before 0.8.6 allows directory traversal, with resultant remote code execution, via the image parameter to the PUT /datastore/image endpoint, as exploited in the wild starting in September 2026.

t: Pozeiden: SVG output injection (stored XSS) via click href, style/classDef colors, %%{init}%% theme variables, and quadrant labels
d: Pozeiden is a MermaidJS renderer written in Zig. Prior to 0.3.0, Pozeiden emits attacker-controlled Mermaid values into SVG attributes or markup without sufficient XML escaping or URL scheme validation, and first-party consumers such as zigmark and policypress embed the generated SVG raw into HTML. The click href syntax can introduce a dangerous URL scheme or break out of an attribute; style, classDef, ::: class assignment, and linkStyle color values can inject fill or stroke markup; color and font-weight values can escape text attributes; %%{init}%% themeVariables can inject global renderer attributes; and quadrant y-axis labels can introduce raw markup. These paths involve src/svg/writer.zig, src/renderers/flowchart.zig, src/renderers/quadrant.zig, and src/root.zig. An attacker who can influence rendered Mermaid source can therefore store script-bearing SVG that executes when another user views the published HTML. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.

t: Pozeiden: Out-of-bounds read/write (crash / memory corruption) on valid diagrams in grid-layout renderers
d: Pozeiden is a MermaidJS renderer written in Zig. Prior to 0.3.0, src/renderers/c4.zig, src/renderers/class.zig, src/renderers/er.zig, and src/renderers/requirement.zig use fixed row-layout arrays while deriving subsequent loop bounds from an untrusted diagram's actual item count, and src/renderers/state.zig indexes a fixed depth array using user-controlled nesting depth. A valid diagram with at least 193 grid items can make the row count exceed the 64-row storage, while a deeply nested state diagram can exceed the col_count depth storage through the public pozeiden.render() path. Safe CLI and ReleaseSafe builds abort the rendering process, enabling reliable denial of service in applications that render untrusted diagrams. ReleaseSmall WASM builds with safety checks disabled instead perform out-of-bounds stack reads or writes, creating a memory-safety violation. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.

t: mcp-ssh-manager: Remote code execution (RCE) via command injection in the backup subsystem
d: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.

t: mcp-ssh-manager: Command injection in mcp-ssh-manager database helpers (ssh_db_list / ssh_db_dump / ssh_db_import)
d: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.6.7, ssh_db_list, ssh_db_dump, ssh_db_import, and ssh_db_restore in src/database-manager.js interpolate caller-controlled database, table, collection, file path, user, host, port, and password values into shell-evaluated command strings without neutralization. Shell metacharacters in these arguments therefore execute arbitrary commands on the configured SSH target as the account used by the MCP server. ssh_db_list is classified as read-only and remains available in readonly and restricted server security modes, so this path bypasses the command-execution boundary those modes are intended to enforce. The dump and import builders are blocked in readonly mode but remain vulnerable in the default unrestricted mode. The earlier version 3.6.5 hardening covered only ssh_db_query query text; it did not protect the list, dump, import, or restore builders, or the connection flags used by query builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.7.

Rocket.Chat's POST /api/v1/chat.sendMessage endpoint improperly validates nested message properties, allowing authenticated users with standard privileges to inject arbitrary message metadata that is persisted and trusted by the server and clients. This can lead to persistent room-level denial of service, stored HTML/iframe injection, unauthorized modification of other users' private starred messages, permission bypass and attribution spoofing for pinned messages, forged edit attribution, and invisible user mentions.

t: isomorphic-git: Arbitrary File Write via Symlink
d: isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.

t: isomorphic-git: NTFS .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION alias bypass writes into the active gitdir
d: isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.7, tree-entry validation in src/models/GitTree.js does not reject the Windows NTFS reserved pathname alias .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION. When clone() or checkout materializes an attacker-controlled tree containing this alias on Windows using an NTFS filesystem, the alias resolves to the active .git directory and permits writes to trusted repository metadata instead of a normal worktree directory. A malicious repository or object stream can therefore poison repository configuration, hooks, refs, attributes, or other gitdir state. Strict hosting that rejects hasDotgit objects can block the crafted tree, and non-NTFS systems do not interpret the pathname as the active gitdir. isomorphic-git performs the gitdir write but does not itself execute the written hook or configuration; a later native Git or compatible-tool action, such as processing a poisoned core.fsmonitor value, can execute configured commands as the victim developer or CI identity. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.7.

t: Avahi: Reachable assertion in dbus_prepare_record_browser_object
d: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc4 and earlier, org.freedesktop.Avahi.Server.RecordBrowserNew accepts a domain-name value that avahi_is_valid_domain_name considers valid even though avahi_normalize_name_strdup cannot normalize it. The resulting null key reaches the key assertion in dbus_prepare_record_browser_object. A local low-privileged D-Bus client can trigger the mismatch and terminate the Avahi daemon, causing denial of service. The issue is fixed in 0.9-rc5.

t: avahi-daemon crashes on receiving resource records where names contain bytes >= 128 (on NetBSD)
d: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc4 and earlier on NetBSD architectures such as x86_64 where char is signed and the ctype guard-page change is present, avahi_domain_hash can pass a negative value to tolower when a resource-record name contains a byte at or above 128. The invalid ctype input reliably raises SIGSEGV, allowing a remote peer on the local network to crash the Avahi daemon. This issue is fixed with 0.9-rc5.

t: pmo-platform: eval-viewer (pmo-skill-refiner): symlink-following arbitrary file read, verbatim secret/PII embedding, and CSRF write on the local review server
d: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py and viewer.html contain three security weaknesses in the local evaluation viewer. During workspace scanning and generation, _find_runs_recursive and build_run follow symlinks and embed_file reads their targets without confining resolved paths to the workspace, although the server do_GET path is not a traversal surface. embed_file also reads output files without a size cap or redaction, allowing secrets or personally identifiable information to be embedded in a no-auth locally served page or shareable static file. Separately, do_POST /api/feedback writes caller-supplied JSON without authentication, an Origin check, or a cross-site request forgery token, allowing a malicious page or DNS-rebound localhost target to modify feedback while the server runs. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.

t: pmo-platform: Warn-mode security hooks fail open (skip their check) when a co-shipped awk primitive is absent
d: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, core/hooks/block-fragile-refs.sh and core/hooks/block-gh-path-leak.sh source co-shipped awk primitives from core/hooks/lib/ and degrade when a required primitive is absent. In a partial or corrupted deployment, block-gh-path-leak.sh skips its entire path-leak check, while block-fragile-refs.sh skips only the positional-issue-reference detector and continues running its other detectors. Both hooks operate in a warning posture, so the impact is a skipped warning rather than bypass of an enforcing control, with no established exfiltration or code-execution primitive. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.

t: pmo-platform: Security Hooks Fail Open Because Runtime PATH Excludes Documented jq Install Paths
d: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

t: Network packet reference leak in IPv6 Router Advertisement handling leads to buffer pool exhaustion
d: The IPv6 neighbour discovery code in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c keeps packets that are waiting for address resolution on a per-neighbour pending queue. A queued packet holds two references: the one handed over by the sender and a second one taken by net_ipv6_send_ns() when the packet is put on the queue. The Router Advertisement handler handle_ra_input() popped each packet off the queue and passed it to net_send_data(), relying on a trailing nbr_clear_ns_pending() call to release the queue reference — but that call then found the queue already empty and released nothing, so one reference was leaked for every pending packet flushed on an RA. Router Advertisements are unauthenticated link-local ICMPv6 messages, so any node on the same link can trigger the flush. An attacker can make the leak deterministic by advertising itself as a router without a source link-layer address option, so the victim's neighbour entry stays INCOMPLETE, then inducing the victim to transmit through that next hop (the packet is queued and a neighbour solicitation is sent), leaving the solicitation unanswered and sending a further RA to drain the queue. Each round leaks one struct net_pkt together with its net_buf chain. Leaked packets are never returned to the fixed-size pools, so the loss is permanent for the lifetime of the boot. With CONFIG_NET_PKT_TX_COUNT defaulting to 4 (14 with CONFIG_NET_PKT_LARGE_DEFAULTS), a small number of repetitions exhausts the transmit packet slab and the node stops being able to send any traffic. The impact is availability only: the reference count is always too high, never too low, so no use-after-free or memory corruption arises. The fix moves the flush into a helper, nbr_send_pending(), which releases the queue reference for every packet it takes off the queue before handing the remaining reference to net_send_data(), and releases that one too if the send is refused.

t: Out-of-bounds write in the SMSC911x Ethernet driver when transmitting frames larger than the staging buffer
d: The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO. eth_tx() in drivers/ethernet/eth_smsc911x.c took the frame length from net_pkt_get_len(pkt) and passed it directly to net_pkt_read(pkt, tx_buf, total_len), with no comparison against the size of tx_buf (NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE). net_pkt_read() takes no destination size and only fails when the packet is shorter than the requested length, so any packet longer than the staging buffer was copied past its end. Nothing between the IP layer and the driver bounds the frame to what the link can carry: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c performs no length check, and the IPv6 output path only compares the packet against the interface MTU when CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT is enabled (it is disabled by default). The size the stack will build is therefore governed by the interface MTU, and that MTU is remotely settable: handle_ra_input() in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c honours the MTU option of any Router Advertisement with a value up to 0xffff, gated only by the standard hop-limit-255 and link-local-source checks. An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can raise the MTU and then have the device emit a single frame of several kilobytes, for example as a TCP segment from any service that returns more than ~1.5 KB or as an oversized UDP datagram. The result is an out-of-bounds write into .bss immediately after tx_buf, with the overrun length and much of its content derived from the transmitted frame. Consequences range from corruption of adjacent kernel data and a crash to potential control-flow influence where the clobbered globals hold pointers; the practical overrun size is bounded by the network buffer pool rather than by the advertised MTU. The fix rejects frames larger than NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with -EMSGSIZE before any TX_DATA_PORT write, so the controller FIFO is also not left holding a command word without its payload.

t: Reference-count underflow in Zephyr network interface address removal releases an IP address that is still in use
d: net_if_ipv4_addr_rm() and net_if_ipv6_addr_rm() in subsys/net/ip/net_if.c unconditionally called net_if_addr_unref() on the target address. When an earlier removal could not complete because another subsystem still held a reference (the TCP stack takes one on the local address of every connection, in tcp_conn_new() and on connect()), the address is left in place with is_added cleared and is_used still set. A second removal of such an address decremented the reference count again, consuming a reference owned by that other holder. When it was the last one, the address slot was released, its NET_EVENT_IPV*_ADDR_DEL event fired, and the slot became reusable while the holder still believed it owned a reference. Every address lookup helper matches on is_used and not on is_added, so a half-removed address stays visible to the rest of the stack and repeat removals are readily reachable from remote input. Under IPv6 SLAAC, an on-link node that sends a Router Advertisement with a short valid lifetime causes the address to expire into the deferred state; a refreshing Router Advertisement is handled by net_if_ipv6_addr_update_lifetime(), which re-arms the lifetime timer without restoring the reference, so the next expiry performs the second, reference-stealing removal. With CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ACD and DHCPv4, repeated spoofed ARP conflicts for the device's lease drive dhcpv4_acd_event_handler() into calling net_if_ipv4_addr_rm() more than once on the same address. Where CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled, the net_if_ipv4_addr_rm_by_index() and net_if_ipv6_addr_rm_by_index() system calls let an unprivileged user-mode thread trigger the same kernel-side release deterministically. The impact is loss of a configured IP address while connections are still using it, and a corrupted reference count that propagates: the slot can be handed to a newly added address, and when the stale holder later tears down, net_if_addr_unref() resolves the address by value and drops the new incarnation's only reference, removing a live address a second time. The affected objects are static array slots and the counter is never decremented below zero, so there is no memory corruption or information disclosure; the consequence is denial of service against the device's network connectivity, repeatable at the attacker's pace. The fix resolves the address before touching the reference count and returns false without calling net_if_addr_unref() when the address is already marked as removed, so the public removal API can no longer consume a reference it does not own.

t: pmo-platform: Stored XSS in Eval Viewer via Unescaped JSON Embedded in Script Context
d: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. From 3.48 until 3.69.1, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py reads untrusted model or skill output from workspace/run*/outputs/ and embeds it with json.dumps into viewer.html inside an inline script without escaping HTML metacharacters. A crafted output can close the script element and execute JavaScript when an operator generates and opens the viewer. The maintainer also confirmed that DOM-based injection through renderGrades and renderBenchmark innerHTML survives transport-only escaping, so affected render sinks must neutralize the content. Executed script can read embedded prompts and outputs, alter the viewer DOM, or modify saved feedback. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

t: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
d: AIT GUI provides a framework for building custom websites for real-time telemetry monitoring, commanding, and other mission operations. From 1.0.0 until 2.5.1, POST /tlm/query in ait/gui/__init__.py writes attacker-controlled field data to fields_in.txt, and its no-PCAP error path can abort before deleting that file. The unauthenticated POST /script/run route accepts a scriptPath that resolves outside ScriptRoot, reads the selected file, and executes it as Python. A network-reachable attacker can obtain the ordinary session cookie without credentials, combine the two routes, and execute arbitrary Python code with the AIT-GUI server process privileges. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.1.

t: Logto: Account takeover via email_verified bypass in social account linking (Azure AD, OAuth2 connectors)
d: Logto is the modern, open-source auth infrastructure for SaaS and AI apps. Prior to 1.46.0, social account linking can use an unverified email returned by the standard OAuth 2.0 or Azure AD connector to select an existing local account. When findSocialRelatedUser matches a victim's email and a request to POST /api/experience/identification enables linkSocialIdentity, an attacker who controls that unverified provider email can link an attacker-controlled social identity to the victim account and sign in as the victim. The issue applies when the provider does not verify email ownership or allows the value to be set freely; Google, GitHub, and default OIDC connector behavior is not affected because those paths expose only verified email. Version 1.46.0 adds an opt-in email synchronization control to the standard OAuth 2.0 connector, while the Azure AD connector has offered an equivalent opt-in control since version 1.43.0. These controls preserve existing behavior by default, so administrators must enable them on affected connectors. A configurable mitigation is available in version 1.46.0.

t: Dnsmasq: dhcpv6 relay remote crash via stale pointer in relay_upstream6()
d: A flaw was found in dnsmasq, where a memory handling issue exists in its Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 (DHCPv6) relay processing. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a sequence of network packets to a system configured as a DHCPv6 relay. This causes the service to write data to previously freed memory and crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

t: Corosync: corosync: heap-based buffer overflow in memb_commit_token handling when msg_len exceeds commit_token_storage
d: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in Corosync's Totem SRP membership commit token handling. The sanity check for memb_commit_token messages validates only minimum length and address-entry counts, not an upper bound against the fixed commit_token_storage buffer. A network-adjacent attacker who can deliver a crafted oversized commit token to a node in the GATHER membership state may overflow the heap-allocated totemsrp instance, leading to memory corruption and denial of service.

t: Quarkus-rest-jsonb: deeply nested json-b bodies cause large stack-trace logs in quarkus rest
d: A flaw was found in the quarkus-rest-jsonb component of Quarkus. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP requests containing deeply nested JSON payloads to vulnerable endpoints. The application fails during JSON parsing and records an excessively large error trace for each small request. This disproportionate log amplification can exhaust system disk space or overwhelm log processing pipelines, degrading service availability.

t: @fastify/reply-from vulnerable to request smuggling via an unsatisfied forwarded Content-Length
d: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards an incoming HTTP request to an upstream server. In versions before 12.9.1, when the plugin forwards a request whose body is not written to the upstream connection, such as a GET, HEAD, or TRACE request that carried a body, or a request with a falsy JSON body, it still forwards the client's Content-Length header while sending no body. The upstream server then treats the bytes of the following request as the unfinished body, which an attacker can use to desynchronize the connection and smuggle a request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.9.1, and users should upgrade to 12.9.1 or later.

t: LinkAce: Private Bookmark URL Existence Oracle via HTML Import Skipped-Count Leaks Other Users Private Links
d: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the HTML bookmark import action in app/Actions/ImportHtmlBookmarks.php uses the global Link::whereUrl() lookup instead of restricting duplicate detection to the importing user. An authenticated user can submit a chosen URL and distinguish the skipped response count from the queued count to learn whether any account has saved that URL, including as a PRIVATE bookmark. The oracle reveals URL existence but does not directly return the bookmark contents or owner. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

t: LinkAce: IDOR on Authenticated Atom Feed Endpoints Exposes Private List and Tag Names Without Authorization Check
d: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

t: LinkAce: Mass Assignment via user_id in API Link Update Allows Ownership Transfer and Content Injection
d: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, LinkController::update() in app/Http/Controllers/API/LinkController.php passes $request->all() to the repository update method even though user_id is fillable and is not an allowed field in the validated update request. An authenticated API user who is authorized to update a link can therefore assign an arbitrary or nonexistent user_id, transferring the link into another user's bookmark collection or orphaning it from any real account. The web update controller is unaffected because it passes only validated fields. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

t: LinkAce: Authenticated visibility-authorization bypass in GET /api/v2/lists/{list}/links discloses other users' private links
d: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.5.9, the authenticated GET /api/v2/lists/{list}/links endpoint in app/Http/Controllers/API/ListLinksController.php authorizes access only to the parent list and then returns its links without applying visibleForUser(). Because another user's INTERNAL or PUBLIC list may legitimately contain PRIVATE links, a normal authenticated user who may view the list can also receive those private link records, including their URLs, titles, descriptions, icons, and timestamps. Equivalent web, tag, notes, and feed handlers apply the per-link visibility scope, so this API handler is the affected exception. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.9.

t: WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging <= 0.9.134 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Migration Receiver and Backup Cleanup
d: The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in version up to, and including, 0.9.134. This is due to a timing side channel in the bundled RSA decryption path, insufficient validation of migration receiver backup records, and missing path validation in the cleanup_local_backup() function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover an active migration receiver's RSA modulus, inject a backup record containing path traversal, and cause a later scheduled cleanup to delete an attacker-selected file writable by the web server. Exploitation requires an unexpired receiver key generated by an administrator and a subsequent manual or scheduled backup lifecycle.

t: Netatalk: RCE - Heap out-of-bounds write in `get_eacontent()` (AppleDouble EA backend) leading to remote code execution in `afpd`
d: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.1.0 until 4.5.2, get_eacontent in libatalk/vfs/ea_ad.c subtracts MAX_REPLY_EXTRA_BYTES from a client-controlled FPGetExtAttr MaxReplySize without rejecting values from 1 through 5, and a signed-to-unsigned comparison can then select an untrusted AppleDouble ea_size. An authenticated client on a volume configured with ea = ad can use a pre-existing malformed AppleDouble sidecar to make read copy attacker-controlled bytes beyond dsi->data + 6 into the surrounding struct DSI, including protocol callback pointers. The malformed sidecar must already exist or be created through a separate local, co-export, management, restore, or vulnerability-assisted write path, and practical code execution depends on the target architecture, structure layout, and address uncertainty; runtime command execution was demonstrated on one x86-64 build. Volumes using ea = sys, ea = none, or ea = auto when it resolves to native system xattrs do not reach this path. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

t: Netatalk: Spotlight mdssvc: NULL-pointer dereference in RPC request handlers
d: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, the Spotlight RPC consumer handlers sl_rpc_fetchAttributeNamesForOIDArray, sl_rpc_storeAttributesForOIDArray, and sl_rpc_fetchAttributesForOIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c dereference the first element of a decoded sl_cnids_t without checking whether the inner CNID array is empty. An authenticated AFP client, or a guest when guest AFP access is enabled, can send a crafted SPOTLIGHT_CMD_RPC whose outer CNIDS length is greater than 16 while its inner count is zero, causing sl_unpack_cnids to create an empty DALLOC_CTX and the consumer to dereference dd_talloc_array[0]. The affected afpd child crashes, normally limiting denial of service to the attacker's session, and no memory write or code execution was demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

t: Netatalk: Spotlight sl_createCNIDArray(): type-confusion heap out-of-bounds read on mixed-type kMDQueryItemArray
d: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, sl_createCNIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c assumes every element of kMDQueryItemArray points to an eight-byte uint64_t and copies sizeof(uint64_t) bytes from the indexed p->dd_talloc_array element without validating the element's talloc type or allocation size. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can use FPSpotlightRPC to supply a mixed-type sl_array_t containing a shorter boolean, nil, or string element, and an unauthenticated client can reach the same path when the optional guest UAM and a guest-accessible volume are enabled. The resulting eight-byte read extends beyond the shorter element's heap allocation and supplies an internal CNID filter; no confidentiality channel, write primitive, or code execution was demonstrated, while a production crash would require additional heap placement conditions. The container-type validation added for CVE-2023-42464 does not validate each element inside an accepted sl_array_t and therefore does not resolve this issue. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

t: Netatalk: afpd DHX2 UAM pre-authentication use-after-free and double-free via repeated FPLoginCont
d: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.0.0 until 4.5.1, the DHX2 and DHX2-PAM authentication state machine in etc/uams/uams_dhx2_pam.c permits logincont1 to be invoked again with the same FPLoginCont retID after it has released the global gcry_mpi_t Ra object. When DHX2 or DHX2PAM is enabled in the UAM list, a remote attacker without valid AFP credentials can repeat the first continuation step, causing gcry_mpi_powm to dereference the freed Ra value and gcry_mpi_release to free it again in a privileged afpd worker. The demonstrated result is a repeatable pre-authentication worker crash, and the use-after-free and double-free provide a plausible allocator exploitation primitive although code execution was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.

t: Netatalk: afpd unauthenticated DSI request smuggling via silent dsi_len truncation in dsi_tcp_open()
d: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_tcp_open in libatalk/dsi/dsi_tcp.c silently limits the bytes read from an unauthenticated DSI frame received on TCP/548 to server_quantum when the attacker-controlled dsi_len is larger, without rejecting the frame or draining the declared remainder. The same silent dsi_len truncation pattern exists in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c. The leftover bytes remain queued on the TCP connection and the next dsi_stream_receive call interprets them as a new DSI header and payload, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to smuggle one or more additional attacker-controlled DSI frames into the same connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.

t: Netatalk: afpd authenticated DSIWrite request smuggling due to missing dsi_doff <= dsi_len validation
d: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_stream_receive in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c independently clamps dsi_doff and dsi_len for DSIWrite requests without enforcing that the data offset is no greater than the declared frame length. An authenticated AFP client can send dsi_doff greater than dsi_len, causing the receiver to consume bytes from a queued subsequent frame before libatalk/dsi/dsi_write.c detects the inconsistency. The irreversible stream desynchronization lets the attacker control the next parsed DSI header and payload and corrupts protocol framing for the connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.
