t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in XOne's XOneManager
d: Authorization bypass in the publication of XOneManager 3.8.3.0 updates. During testing, the server accepted initial requests from an authenticated project member with read-only access without verifying publication permissions. If the workflow is completed, updates with modified content could be distributed to managed devices.

t: flowintel DOM-based XSS via Timeline Autolinking, Search Highlighting, and Content-Type Confusion
d: flowintel contains multiple related flaws that allow an authenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML or script into pages viewed by other users. - Timeline rendering: the timeline library's autolinking feature rewrote already-sanitised case notes and imported MISP attribute values into generated HTML link elements. Crafted text containing quote characters could break out of the generated attribute context, altering the surrounding markup and enabling script execution in the victim's browser. - Search highlighting: the highlight injection logic used a regular expression to locate text between angle brackets and spliced <mark> elements into the resulting string. Because the pattern could match inside HTML attribute values, the rewrite could corrupt or inject content into attributes of already-sanitised markup, again leading to DOM-based cross-site scripting. - Content-Type confusion: three analyser selection endpoints returned session-stored JSON strings with a text/html content type. A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context. Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated user with the ability to create or import case content (notes, MISP attributes) containing specially crafted quote or angle-bracket sequences. The victim must subsequently open the affected case timeline, run a search, or request one of the selection endpoints. Impact: successful exploitation yields DOM-based cross-site scripting in the victim's browser session, potentially allowing disclosure of case data, session manipulation, or execution of arbitrary actions under the victim's identity. Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

t: flowintel Information Disclosure of Webhook Secrets and Logs to Non-Admin Users
d: flowintel contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to access sensitive configuration data and logs intended for administrators only. The notification page and alert API responses exposed sensitive fields, including webhook URLs, signing secrets, IMAP credentials, and delivery logs, in the initial data or JSON responses. Although the user interface hid the configuration form from non-admin users, the underlying data remained accessible via the page source or API endpoints. This exposure included historical webhook URLs that may contain active bearer tokens. An attacker with a valid non-admin account could retrieve these credentials and logs, potentially leading to unauthorized access to notification services, impersonation of the application in webhook deliveries, or further lateral movement within the infrastructure. Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

t: flowintel Insecure Direct Object Reference Allows Cross-Case Data Access and Modification
d: flowintel contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability affecting multiple endpoints that manage child records of cases and tasks. An authenticated user with access to one case or task could read or modify records belonging to other cases by supplying identifiers of those records directly in the request. Affected operations include: - Reading task notes, subtasks, and URL tools by referencing their IDs without verifying they belong to the authorized task - Retrieving task assignees for a task belonging to a different case - Editing or deleting timeline events and timeline event links belonging to another case - Editing or removing case connectors belonging to another case - Invoking connector module operations (MISP, generic connectors, worker calls) by combining an authorized case with a connector link from a different case The root cause is that the application authorized the parent resource (case or task) in the URL but then fetched or operated on the child record independently without verifying the child's ownership relationship to the authorized parent. Security impact: an authenticated user can exfiltrate sensitive threat intelligence data from cases they do not have access to, and can modify or delete timeline entries, connector configurations, and other records in unauthorized cases, leading to data integrity loss and potential disruption of incident response workflows. Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0

t: flowintel Analyzer: Missing Authorization on Result Reads and Case/Task Writes (IDOR)
d: flowintel contains multiple authorization bypass vulnerabilities in its Analyzer (MISP Modules) functionality, affecting both the web interface and the REST API. - Saving analyzer results to a case or task accepted caller-supplied case and task identifiers without verifying that the authenticated user is a member of the target case or holds the required restricted-task permissions. An authenticated user could write notes, create tasks, and attach MISP objects or attributes into another organization's case. - Stored analyzer results were retrievable by UUID by any authenticated user. Both the web endpoint and the API endpoint returned the full result payload without checking ownership, exposing another user's analysis output. - The save handler did not validate the structure of the request, did not reject conflicting destination selections, and did not halt processing when a task-note operation failed, allowing partial or unintended writes. Preconditions: the attacker must possess a valid authenticated session (or API token) in flowintel. No administrative role is required. Security impact: unauthorized cross-tenant data disclosure (analyzer results) and unauthorized cross-tenant data modification (notes, tasks, MISP objects/attributes in another organization's case). Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

t: FlowIntel: Missing Authorization and Credential Scope Enforcement in Connector and Template Features
d: FlowIntel contains multiple authorization and credential management vulnerabilities affecting connector instances, MISP helper tools, and case templates. - Connector instance metadata, connectivity checks, and case listings accepted instance IDs without verifying if the acting user had visibility or ownership rights, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive configuration and data. - Case template serialization and creation processes exposed connector instances attached to templates regardless of the user's permissions, potentially leaking credentials or instance details to users who should not have access. - Editing connector instances allowed changes to URLs or sharing scopes without requiring re-authentication of API keys, enabling the reuse of another user's credentials in a new context or the leakage of shared keys to unauthorized endpoints. - Outbound MISP connector keys were incorrectly accepted for authenticating incoming alerts, bypassing the intended separation between outbound integration credentials and inbound alert source authentication. These issues allow authenticated users to access unauthorized connector data, manipulate credential scopes, and potentially exploit credential confusion between different security contexts. Affected versions: < 4.1.0

t: FlowIntel Cross-Organisation User Directory and Assignment Information Disclosure
d: FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass in its user directory and assignment endpoints that allows authenticated users to access data belonging to other organisations. When the LIMIT_USER_VIEW_TO_ORG setting is enabled to restrict directory visibility to the caller's organisation, several API endpoints (user lookup by ID, last name, Matrix ID, and role-based listings) did not consistently enforce the organisation boundary. An authenticated non-admin user could retrieve profiles of users in other organisations by supplying their identifiers. Additionally, OrgAdmin users could retrieve the task assignments of any user in the system, including tasks and case titles from private cases to which they had no access. The assignment endpoints did not verify that the requested user belonged to the caller's organisation or that the underlying cases were visible to the caller. Security impact: - Exposure of user identities (names, Matrix IDs, roles) across organisation boundaries - Disclosure of task assignments, case titles, and workflow details from private cases - Potential enumeration of other organisations' membership and case activity Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in XOne's XOneManager
d: Authorization omission in the 'admusers' operation of the POST request to '/xmanagercore/api/services/' in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. The API fails to verify the required role for querying the directory. An authenticated member of the project can obtain the list of platform accounts—including administrative accounts—along with details such as email addresses, roles, and associated companies.

t: Flowintel SSO Identity and Organisation Trust Boundary Violations Allow Account Takeover, Privilege Escalation, and Unauthorized Case Access
d: Flowintel contains multiple SSO identity and organisation trust boundary violations that collectively allow account takeover, privilege escalation, and unauthorized access to private case data. - Keycloak SSO accepted unverified email claims, and all SSO providers (Keycloak, Entra ID, SimpleSAML) could resolve a claimed email address to an existing account that was created via a different sign-in method, enabling cross-provider account collision and unauthorized access to another user's account and data. - Entra ID role mapping relied on group display names, which tenant members could duplicate by creating a group with the same name as a privileged group (e.g. FlowintelAdmin), resulting in unauthorized role escalation. - SSO provisioning reused organisations whose display names matched user-controlled profile names, granting the new SSO user access to that organisation's private cases without explicit administrator assignment. - Case sharing via the API resolved organisations by name using a first-match query, so ambiguous names could silently resolve to the wrong organisation. Preconditions: an attacker must have a valid SSO identity (Keycloak, Entra ID, or SimpleSAML) or be a member of the relevant Entra tenant. No local administrator access is required. Security impact: unauthorized access to private case data, privilege escalation to Editor or higher roles, and account takeover across authentication providers. Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

t: Flowintel Matrix Relay Authorization Bypass Allows Privilege Escalation and Bot Impersonation
d: Flowintel contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in its Matrix relay (bot) integration. When the relay forwarded API requests on behalf of a represented user, the authorization and permission checks evaluated the relay bot's elevated role while the request handlers acted as the lower-privileged represented user. This mismatch allowed users with restricted roles (e.g., Read Only) to perform write operations, directory lookups, calendar modifications, assignment changes, template creation, and import actions they were not authorized to perform. Additionally, relay authority was determined by matching editable user profile fields (name and email) rather than a protected, non-spoofable identifier. An ordinary user who modified their profile to match the expected bot name could be recognized as the trusted relay, enabling impersonation of the bot and potential access to its elevated privileges. Preconditions: - A valid Flowintel user account with a restricted role (e.g., Read Only) - Access to the Matrix relay integration or the ability to send API requests with the relay's API key and a MATRIX-ID header - For the impersonation vector: ability to edit one's own profile name fields Security impact: - Unauthorized write operations by users with read-only or otherwise restricted permissions - Potential impersonation of the trusted relay bot by ordinary users - Bypass of organization-level access controls and role-based restrictions - Unauthorized modification of cases, tasks, calendar events, templates, and user directory entries Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0

t: Exploitation of Weak or Known Passwords in Danfoss AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series
d: The Danfoss legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series are vulnerable to unauthorized access when default credentials or known passwords are used for authentication. These products were manufactured with default credentials documented in the product manual. All versions are affected.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in XOne's XOneManager

An authenticated project member can execute SQL queries using ‘filter’ without the server verifying their execution permissions. The queries use the service account’s permissions. During testing, databases outside the project were queried, including the authentication database.

t: Apache Texera: Authenticated users can always see and modify other's workflow execution results

This allows any authenticated user to read or modify any other user's workflow execution results. This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue.

t: Stack-based buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM8xxA unauthenticated CGI handler

Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

t: Flowintel Session Identifiers Not Bound to Credentials Allow Persistent Access After Password Change
d: Flowintel , contained a session management vulnerability in its browser authentication mechanism. The session identifier used a bare numeric user ID rather than a credential-bound token, resulting in several related weaknesses: - Remembered logins (remember-me cookies) remained valid after a user changed their password, allowing an attacker holding a previously issued cookie to retain access indefinitely. - Server-side session identifiers were not rotated upon login (local, SSO, or remembered), enabling session fixation. - Self-service email and password changes did not require verification of the current password, permitting an attacker with an active session to modify account credentials without knowledge of the existing password. - Administrator-initiated password resets did not revoke other browser sessions, invalidate remembered logins, or rotate the affected user's API key. An attacker who obtained a valid session or remember-me cookie (e.g., through XSS, network interception, or cookie theft) could maintain unauthorized access even after the legitimate user changed their password. Additionally, an attacker with any valid session could change the account's email address or password without knowing the current credentials, effectively taking over the account. Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

t: FlowIntel CSRF via GET-accepted destructive web routes bypassing Flask-WTF protection
d: FlowIntel contained a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability affecting fourteen web routes that performed destructive or state-changing operations. The affected routes accepted HTTP GET requests in addition to (or instead of) POST, which bypassed the Flask-WTF CSRF token validation that is only enforced on non-GET requests. The vulnerable operations included: - Case deletion and case merging - Organisation removal from a case - Task deletion (case and template) - Case template and note template deletion - Connector, connector instance, and icon deletion - Custom tag deletion and status change - Taxonomy and galaxy status changes An attacker who could induce an authenticated user to follow a crafted link or load a page containing a cross-site navigation (e.g., an image tag or redirect) could trigger any of these destructive actions using the victim's session cookie, without the victim's explicit consent or awareness. No special privileges beyond a valid authenticated session with the appropriate role (editor or admin) were required on the victim's account. Security impact: unauthorized deletion or modification of cases, tasks, templates, connectors, icons, custom tags, taxonomies, and galaxies belonging to the victim or the organisation, resulting in loss of data integrity. Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

t: Flowintel Disables TLS Certificate Verification for MISP and Mail Connections
d: Flowintel disabled TLS certificate verification for all MISP API connections and used unverified SSL contexts for IMAP and SMTP STARTTLS mail connections. This allowed an on-path (man-in-the-middle) attacker positioned between Flowintel and its MISP or mail servers to impersonate the remote server and intercept sensitive data. Affected connections include: - All MISP HTTPS API calls (event retrieval, attribute search, event creation, connectivity checks, and API validation) - SMTP STARTTLS connections used for sending email notifications - IMAP TLS connections used for fetching mail archives and testing connectivity An attacker who can observe or intercept network traffic between Flowintel and the MISP or mail server could: - Capture MISP API keys and mail credentials (SMTP/IMAP passwords) - Read all threat intelligence data exchanged (events, attributes, objects, reports) - Inject or modify threat intelligence data returned to Flowintel The vulnerability required no authentication on the part of the attacker and no user interaction; it was exploitable by any party with a network position between Flowintel and its configured MISP or mail endpoints. Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in XOne's XOneManager
d: Authorization bypass via a user-controlled key in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. The 'ConvertBDToProject' operation selects the database based on 'databasename' without verifying the user’s permissions on it. An authenticated user can link a project to a database outside their scope and identify existing databases based on API responses.

d: MsgPack and NNTP protocol dissector crashes in 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19 allows denial of service

The server processes POST requests to ‘/xmanagercore/api/Project/ConvertBDToProject/’ without verifying the administrative role. Certain EZVIZ devices are affected by a replay attack vulnerability (CWE-294). An attacker may intercept communication traffic and replay specific control commands, causing the device to execute unauthorized operations.

t: Pie Register <= 3.8.4.17 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Administrator Role Modification via Oversized 'username' Parameter
d: The Pie Register – User Registration, Profiles & Content Restriction plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.17 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the role of the site's primary administrator account (user ID 1) with the registration form's configured role, demoting the administrator to a lower-privileged role and locking them out of wp-admin. This vulnerability is exploitable only on PHP 8+, where casting a WP_Error object to int yields 1, causing the role modification to target user ID 1.
r: Pie Register – User Registration, Profiles & Content Restriction

t: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes <= 4.5.5 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'ajax_pagination_referrer' Parameter on /ngg_tag/<tag>/
d: The NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 via the 'ajax_pagination_referrer' request parameter used on the /ngg_tag/<tag>/ taxonomy page. This is due to the plugin reading the pagination base URL from $_REQUEST, preserving the attacker-supplied host on the tag route (where ngg_wprouting_add_post_permalink is forced to false so the plugin does not re-base the links to the site's own permalink), and caching the fully rendered page in a transient keyed only on the request URI (not the request body) for 1800 seconds via NGG_RENDERING_CACHE / PHOTOCRATI_CACHE. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to poison the cached /ngg_tag/<tag>/ page so that its pagination links point to an attacker-controlled host; the plugin's own ajax_pagination.
r: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery

t: Mega Forms <= 1.7.9 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Submitted Field Value
d: The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
r: Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic

t: CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) <= 4.6.2 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'courier_code' and 'tracking_number' Parameters via REST Auth Bypass
d: The CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[].courier_code, data[].tracking_number (plus pp_sign for the auth bypass)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The authentication bypass is reachable only when the parcelpanel_api_key WordPress option is non-empty, which occurs automatically once an admin has opened or connected the ParcelPanel admin page; at that point any unauthenticated attacker can bypass the sole access gate by supplying a JSON boolean true as pp_sign, which PHP's loose == operator coerces to true when compared against the non-empty md5 hex string.
r: CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce

t: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes <= 4.5.5 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via Smilie-to-Lightbox Caption
d: The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the plugin's "What must the lightbox be applied to?" setting (thumbEffectContext) to be configured as "Try to apply to all images" or "Try to apply to all images that link to image files," which is not the shipping default, and also requires the attacker's comment to reach a publicly rendered state.
r: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery

t: Nexter Extension <= 4.9.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation to 'reset-view' Parameter
d: The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the role_switcher_to_view_admin_as() function handling the `reset-view` branch without a capability check or nonce when the caller's own login is supplied, combined with an incomplete cleanup hook (maybe_prevent_switchback_to_administrator) that exits early when the user's current roles equal the stored view role and that is never triggered when WordPress core's WP_User::set_role() short-circuits because the account already has only the target role. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to Administrator.
r: Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit

t: Mang Board <= 2.4.7 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Content Deletion via 'mode' / 'comment_pid' / 'board_pid' Parameter Confusion
d: The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.7. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete any board post — including administrator-owned content — along with its associated comments and file links. A nonce sufficient to pass the initial nonce check is publicly exposed on any board listing page, meaning no prior authentication or privileged access is required to initiate the exploit.

t: Hydrogen Calendar Embeds <= 3.0.3 - Unauthenticated Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via ICS Feed Event Fields (SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION)
d: The Hydrogen Calendar Embeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via ICS Feed Event Fields (SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION) in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the attacker to have write access to an ICS feed that has been configured as a calendar source on the target WordPress site.

t: My Calendar <= 3.8.13 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'event_street' Address Field
d: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_street' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level users via the plugin's Permissions settings; once granted, the Subscriber can store the payload without the mc_edit_locations capability because mc_admin_save() does not enforce it before calling mc_insert_location().

t: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes <= 4.5.5 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via IPTC/EXIF Image Metadata
d: The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'IPTC 2#120 (caption) / 2#005 (title) inside the image file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an authenticated user with image-edit permissions to import an attacker-supplied image file, which is the plugin's standard workflow for photographer uploads, client galleries, and contest submissions.
r: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery

t: My Calendar <= 3.8.13 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'event_post' Parameter
d: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_post (post ID) + event_title (XSS payload) + content (shortcode)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level or other lower-privileged roles, which is the plugin's documented workflow for allowing front-end event submissions.

t: My Calendar <= 3.8.13 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Event Title
d: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mc_template (template body); event_title (payload storage)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the site to have granted mc_add_events to Subscriber-level users (a configurable plugin permission), and relies on a privileged user — such as an Administrator — following the event preview link surfaced on the My Calendar Events management screen.

t: My Calendar <= 3.8.13 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Event Title
d: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's documented permission grant to be applied, which allows Subscriber-level users to add and publish events; once granted, a self-submitted event title containing an entity-encoded payload is auto-published and fires in any visitor's browser upon clicking the event on the public calendar.

t: Mang Board <= 2.4.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal via 'file_path' Parameter
d: The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal in versions up to, and including, 2.4.8 via the `file_path` column handled by the `mbw_board_files_api_body()` function. The plugin stores an attacker-supplied value directly into the files admin table (no realpath, dot-segment, or directory-containment filtering) and later concatenates it onto `MBW_UPLOAD_PATH` before passing the result to `@unlink()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including `wp-config.

t: Unverified key-pair binding lets an unauthenticated token user substitute the public key or certificate returned for a private key
d: In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the key-pair and certificate lookup functions (`FindKeyPair`, `FindKeyPairs`, `FindKeyPairsWithAttributes`, `FindAllKeyPairs`, the `FindRSAKeyPair*` family and `FindAllPairedCertificates`) pair a private key with a public key object, or with a certificate, by `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` alone, take the first match the token returns, and never verify that it belongs to the private key. PKCS#11 permits a session that has not logged in to create public token objects, so anyone able to open a session on the token — without the PIN — can plant a public key or certificate carrying a victim key's `CKA_ID` and label, and crypto11 may return it as that key's public half. An application that publishes or trusts `Signer.Public()` (a JWKS endpoint, a key registry, `authorized_keys`, a CSR) then publishes the attacker's key, and relying parties accept anything the attacker signs as coming from the service. On the v1 line the lookup also falls back to a class-and-key-type-only search when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, pairing a label-only private key with the first public key of its type on the token. The v1 module paths are deprecated and will not be fixed; users should migrate to github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2 version 2.0.0-rc9 or later.

t: FlowIntel Insecure Note Variable Resolution, Over-Permissive Chatbot API Access, and Credential Exposure in Process Arguments
d: FlowIntel contains multiple security flaws in its note variable resolution, chatbot API tooling, and AI report generation. - Note variable references (e.g. cross-case or cross-task lookups) were resolved using the viewing user's privileges rather than the destination case's audience. An authenticated user with access to a shared or imported note could embed references to private cases, causing sensitive case data to be pulled into AI report requests, exports, and MISP sends without the referenced case's audience having granted read access. - The chatbot API tool permitted the language model to invoke any FlowIntel API endpoint, including administrative routes and state-changing GET operations, without an allow-list or path validation. An attacker who can influence the model's instructions (e.g. via untrusted case content) could induce data modification or access restricted endpoints. - AI report generation passed the Ollama bearer token and full case content as command-line arguments to a child process, exposing them in the system process table to any local user. Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.

t: flowintel CI/CD Workflow Exposes Checkout Credentials in Docker Build Cache
d: The flowintel Docker build workflow used the GitHub Actions checkout action with default credential persistence, causing the job authentication token to be written into the repository's Git configuration file. This file became part of the Docker build context and could be retained in exported build cache layers, even though Git metadata was stripped from the final runtime image. An attacker with access to the CI/CD build cache or build environment could extract the persisted token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the private source repository. Impact: - Exposure of a valid authentication token to the private repository - Potential unauthorized read access to source code and repository metadata Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

t: ModelCloud GPTQModel Adapter Resolution Pipeline remote.py gptqmodel.adapter.remote.resolve_path input validation

t: Certmonger: missing size limits and timeouts in scep ca reply handling lead to denial of service
d: A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

t: flowintel Case History Log Injection via Line Separator Characters in User-Authored Fields
d: flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators). An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records. The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access. Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

t: FlowIntel: Resource Exhaustion via Sparse CSV/JSON Table Expansion During File-to-Note Conversion
d: FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU. The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel - Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note Impact: - Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users - No confidentiality or integrity impact Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

t: GitHub Actions pull_request_target code injection in nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee (build_documentation.yml)
d: In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write, pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

t: FV Flowplayer Video Player <= 7.5.57.7212 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'caption' Shortcode Attribute
d: The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's 'Parse Vimeo and YouTube links' setting to be enabled, which wires do_shortcode into the comment_text filter chain and allows the [fvplayer] shortcode to be rendered from comment content.

t: EU Order Withdrawal Button for WooCommerce <= 2.4.6 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via User-Agent Header
d: The EU Order Withdrawal Button for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution requires an Administrator or Shop Manager to open the Withdrawals Preview modal and click the injected note element, which the attacker can enlarge via a retained style attribute to cover the entire note area. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
r: EU Order Withdrawal Button for WooCommerce

t: Events Made Easy <= 3.3.8 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'event[event_notes]' Parameter
d: The Events Made Easy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event[event_notes]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable when the plugin's 'Allow guest submit?' Frontend Submit option is enabled, though the required nonce is freely obtainable by any anonymous visitor as it is printed on every frontend page.

t: FV Flowplayer Video Player <= 7.5.57.7212 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'fv_wp_flowplayer_field_src' Parameter
d: The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[videos][0][fv_wp_flowplayer_field_src]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The fv_player_db_save AJAX endpoint's INSERT path is gated only by a per-user preview nonce and never calls current_user_can(), allowing any authenticated subscriber-level user who possesses their own nonce to store the malicious payload. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that administrator has enabled the plugin option fvwpflowplayer['profile_videos_enable_bio']=true (off by default), which enqueues the shortcode editor and the per-user preview_nonce on wp-admin/profile.php for every logged-in user. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

t: Chatterbug Forms <= 1.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Content-Disposition 'filename='
d: The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_delete_uploaded_files function in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Exploitation requires an administrator to delete the attacker-planted form entry, and the attacker must know or be able to guess the absolute path of a file writable by the PHP process. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

t: Flowintel Template Repository Path Traversal and Symlink Escape Allows Arbitrary File Read
d: Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed: - Repository registration and editing accepted arbitrary local paths without verifying they resolved inside the configured REPOSITORY_BASE_PATH, allowing an authenticated user to point a repository at any readable directory on the host. - Manifest and template file lookups used normalized (non-canonical) path joins and a startswith-based guard that could be bypassed by symbolic links, permitting reads of files outside the intended repository. An authenticated user with the ability to add or edit a template repository could therefore cause the application to read and return the contents of arbitrary files readable by the service account, including configuration files, credentials, or other sensitive data. Affected: Flowintel versions prior to 4.1.0.

t: rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress <= 4.7.17 - Unauthenticated SQL Injection via 'custom_fields' Parameter

This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The upload endpoint's only access control is a nonce check, and the 'rtmedia_upload_nonce' value is localized to every unauthenticated visitor on every front-end page via wp_enqueue_scripts, making it freely obtainable without an account.

t: Toocheke Companion <= 2.38 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Contributor+) Arbitrary Post Deletion via 'series_post_id' Parameter

r: PDF Poster – Let visitors read PDF’s without leaving the page

t: Kognetiks Chatbot <= 2.5.9 - Unauthenticated Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via 'comment' Parameter via MathJax Rendering
d: The Kognetiks Chatbot plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The TeX payload survives WordPress core comment kses intact because it contains no HTML tags, and MathJax is active on fresh installs by default due to the 'chatbot_chatgpt_enable_mathjax' option defaulting to 'Yes' with no page or shortcode presence guard on enqueue.

t: PayPlus Payment Gateway <= 8.3.4 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Arbitrary Order Payment Manipulation via generate-link-payment AJAX Acti
d: The PayPlus Payment Gateway plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 8.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to generate PayPlus payment page links for arbitrary WooCommerce orders belonging to any customer, overwrite those orders' payment method and PayPlus-related order meta, and trigger PayPlus API calls using the store's credentials — including, when a POS EMV device is configured, initiating a charge request to the store's physical POS terminal. The exploit requires no nonce and no special capability beyond being logged in, as the authorization block is unreachable on the AJAX path due to the inverted isset() predicate.

t: Xagio SEO & AEO <= 7.1.0.51 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'title' Shortcode Attribute
d: The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.51 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post filter applied at save time does not strip angle-bracket-free double-quote breakout payloads in shortcode attribute values, leaving injected event handlers intact in stored post content.
r: Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility

t: mozilla-ai llamafile Container llamafile.c llamafile_open_zip out-of-bounds
d: A flaw has been found in mozilla-ai llamafile up to .0.10.5. This issue affects the function llamafile_open_zip of the file llamafile/llamafile.c of the component Container Parser. This manipulation of the argument size causes out-of-bounds read. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 0.10.6 is capable of addressing this issue. t: Open redirect in Mattermost web app landing page sends users to external sites
d: Mattermost versions 11.2.x <= 11.2.4 fail to validate that the redirect target on the web app landing page that prompts users to open links in the desktop app stays on the Mattermost origin which allows an unauthenticated attacker to redirect a user to an arbitrary external site via a crafted link. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00893

t: Flowintel Community Data Launcher Exposes Admin API Key in Child Process Arguments
d: Flowintel's community data launcher script passes the admin API key as a command-line argument to a child Python helper process. On Unix-like systems, process arguments are readable by all local users via standard tools such as ps or by reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline, allowing any local user to observe the key while the helper process is running. An attacker with local access to the host can capture the admin API key during the brief window in which the helper process is active. Possession of the key grants full administrative access to the Flowintel REST API, enabling unauthorized creation, modification, or deletion of threat intelligence data, users, roles, and organisations. Preconditions: - The victim must invoke the community data import or deletion command (launch.sh -tdc or -dtdc) with the API key supplied as a positional argument. - The attacker must have a local user account on the same host and be able to observe process listings during the helper execution window. Impact: - Disclosure of the Flowintel admin API key to any local user. - Subsequent full administrative control over the Flowintel instance via its REST API. Affected: <4.1.0

t: Tool result data shaped like a file is rebuilt as a file download or provider file reference when message history is reloaded
d: When message history is serialized and loaded again, a tool result that contains a JSON object in the serialized shape of one of Pydantic AI's file types is rebuilt as that file. A third party who controls data a tool returns, such as a record that an MCP server or a function tool returns from an external system, can use this to make the application download a URL on its local network, or make the model provider read an s3:// object or uploaded file with the application's credentials. Applications are affected when tool results can contain third-party data, message history containing those results is serialized and loaded again (stored history, history a UI adapter holds on the server, or Temporal, DBOS or Prefect durable execution), and the model is one Pydantic AI downloads files for, one that honors force_download, or one whose provider resolves non-HTTP file URLs or uploaded files. History that a client submits through the Vercel AI or AG-UI adapter in the default mode is not affected. The issue is fixed in pydantic-ai and pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.10 and 2.66.0.

t: Quadratic time timedelta validation in Pydantic V1
d: Validating an untrusted ISO 8601 duration string into a timedelta field with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few dozen kilobytes takes seconds to validate. The iso8601_duration_re regular expression used to parse ISO 8601 durations (in pydantic/datetime_parse.py) contains an unescaped ".", which also matches digits. On a string of digits, the repeated groups overlap and the regex engine backtracks in quadratic time. The issue was fixed in commit 62791e66a9f8f118e465ed760c9e2ede9ae3055e. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into timedelta fields.

t: Quadratic time unique_items list validation in Pydantic V1
d: Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate. The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons. The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()). The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint. Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

t: Validation bypass of aliased fields in TypedDict and dataclasses allowing extra data
d: When extra data is allowed, providing both the alias and the name of an aliased TypedDict or dataclass field makes the unvalidated value (provided under the name) overwrite the validated one (provided under the alias), resulting in validated data not matching the declared type. Extra items are stored in the same dictionary as the fields (the returned dictionary for TypedDict, the instance __dict__ for dataclasses). As only the alias is marked as used, the field name is treated as an extra item, and its unvalidated value overrides the validated one. The TypedDict validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/typed_dict.rs) and the dataclass validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/dataclass.rs) share this logic. The issue was fixed in commit 34491f5328f168f14e3769cd5f0f83c0af0f4778. Impact: validation bypass, as data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into TypedDict or dataclass types with aliased fields and extra data allowed (with extra='allow', or with the extra_items argument for TypedDict), using Pydantic V2 (up to and including 2.14.1). Pydantic models (BaseModel) are not affected, as extra data is stored separately from fields.

t: Unbounded exponent in Fraction validation
d: Validating an untrusted string in exponent notation into a Fraction field computes the full power of ten without any bound: an input of a few bytes takes seconds to validate. String inputs are passed to the Fraction constructor. For strings in exponent notation (e.g. '1e8000000'), CPython computes the corresponding power of ten as an integer (in Lib/fractions.py). The issue was fixed in commit 69ed168e9ad465eef4c8d81efb152a93b604daf5. For strings in exponent notation, the exponent is now parsed before calling the Fraction constructor, and exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into Fraction fields (in both JSON and Python mode, including in strict mode), using Pydantic from 2.10.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.0. From 2.14.0, exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected, matching the maximum number of digits accepted for integers.

t: Quadratic time and memory multi-host URL validation
d: Validating an untrusted URL with a long scheme and many hosts into a multi-host URL field (e.g. PostgresDsn) takes quadratic time and memory: an input of about a hundred kilobytes takes around a gigabyte of memory to validate. The parse_multihost_url() function (in pydantic-core/src/validators/url.rs) parses each host separately, prepending the whole URL prefix (including the scheme) to every one of them. As the scheme can be arbitrarily long, and is parsed and stored once per host, both time and memory grow quadratically with the input size. Allowed schemes (e.g. postgres for PostgresDsn) are only checked after parsing, so they don't prevent the issue. The issue was fixed in commit b4028f9d87e34750e53be0ba011d70f3c0fcc94e. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into multi-host URL fields (PostgresDsn, MongoDsn, NatsDsn, or custom types built on MultiHostUrl).

t: Validation bypass of extra data keys in JSON model validation
d: When validating JSON data into a model allowing extra data, the keys of extra data aren't validated against the key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__, resulting in extra data not matching the declared type. This is the case if you define __pydantic_extra__ as e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r'^x_')], int]. The validate_json_by_iteration() method (in pydantic-core/src/validators/model_fields.rs), used to validate JSON data into models, only validates the values of extra data, and stores the keys as is. The issue was fixed in commit 4c65dbda9970a488e2ff21c8693fc6f6d70a3358. Impact: validation bypass, as extra data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted JSON data into models allowing extra data (with extra='allow'), with a key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__ (e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], int]), using Pydantic from 2.13.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.2. Python mode validation isn't affected.

t: itsourcecode Banking Management System navbar.php cross site scripting
d: A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Banking Management System 1.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file navbar.php. The manipulation of the argument page results in cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.

t: vulnerability-lookup: 2FA Disabled via Unauthenticated GET Request and Unpublished Comments Accessible Without Authorization
d: vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/<uuid>) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public release.

t: Matthias-Wandel jhead PNG Section pngfile.c RemovePngSection double free
d: A security vulnerability has been detected in Matthias-Wandel jhead up to 3.3. This affects the function RemovePngSectionByType/RemovePngSection of the file src/pngfile.c of the component PNG Section Handler. The manipulation leads to double free. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

t: io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free read in this path. Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

t: io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate() When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(), sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during execution. However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type. Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

t: io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind() When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking current->io_uring_restrict. As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in the task's allowed register_op bitmap. Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.

t: io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs bpf_io_uring_submit_sqes() calls io_submit_sqes() from inside the loop program, with current->bpf_ctx set, and requests issued inline run with it set too. The socket code uses has_current_bpf_ctx() to recognize calls from bpf_setsockopt() and friends, where the caller holds the socket lock and has already been vetted, and skips both. So a SOCKET_URING_OP_SETSOCKOPT from the SQ passes sockopt_capable() without the capability, and runs without lock_sock(). A task with no capability can set SO_MARK, IP_TRANSPARENT or TCP_REPAIR, and two threads changing IP_OPTIONS on one socket, one through the ring, double free in no time. SOCK_DESTROY via IORING_OP_SENDMSG ends up in tcp_abort() without the lock the same way. Clear the run context around io_submit_sqes(). The SQEs come from userspace and must be issued like those of any other ring. They still run inside the program's RCU tasks trace read section, so a request that sleeps there holds up that grace period, but other request types do that already.

t: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work() running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else branch: percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1); if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel))) wake_up(&tctx->wait); put_task_struct(tctx->task); The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(), and on exec it frees the tctx right after. Nothing holds that off for the remaining three lines, the task reference only covers a tctx freed along with the task_struct. It used to work out because io_uring_del_tctx_node() took the uring_lock that the freeing side holds across io_put_task(), until that moved to tctx_lock. Free the tctx with kfree_rcu(), and enter an RCU read section in io_put_task() before the count is dropped.

t: io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit. The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64 closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from being freed, for everyone. Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread, and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring, rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash is refcounted.

t: io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work An IOPOLL ring without DEFER_TASKRUN can be reaped by a task other than the one that submitted the I/O. If a polled request is marked REQ_F_REISSUE, io_free_batch_list() calls io_queue_iowq() with the original tctx. Ordinary task exit can tear down tctx->io_wq after draining only the tracked requests. The live request pins the task, but not its io-wq, so the foreign task can race io_wq_put_and_exit() and enqueue through a freed or NULL queue. Forward foreign userspace enqueues to the owning task before accessing tctx->io_wq. Use a dedicated task_work callback so reissues still go straight to io-wq, and fail them if task_work is running in cancellation mode. Preserve the existing PF_KTHREAD cancellation path. This also covers the other callers of io_queue_iowq() without changing the worker-owned enqueue path.

t: io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits An exiting SQPOLL thread calls io_uring_cancel_generic() with sqd->lock held, and keeps it across cond_resched() and the sleep until nothing is in flight anymore. A zero-copy send notification can't be canceled and stays pending as long as the peer doesn't read, so the lock is held for as long as a user cares to. io_ring_exit_work() needs it to park the thread, and so do IORING_REGISTER_IOWQ_AFF and IOWQ_MAX_WORKERS. With 64 such rings sharing the thread, every iou_exit slot sleeps on the lock and no ring gets freed for anyone. Drop the lock around cond_resched() and the sleep, like the main loop of the thread does. Each walk of ctx_list is still under one hold, and nothing is kept across the unlock. The thread drops its io-wq, frees its tctx and clears sqd->thread under one hold after the loop, so whoever holds the lock and finds sqd->thread set can still use them. [axboe: adapted to the schedule_timeout() based loop]

t: io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() calls io_try_cancel() until nothing is found, and io_poll_cancel() cancels one request per call, starting each lookup at the beginning of the hash. A cancelled request stays hashed until its task work runs, so every lookup walks past the ones already cancelled. Cancelling K of N pending polls visits about K*N/2 requests in one io_uring_enter(), with uring_lock held. A single CANCEL_FD|ALL on 80000 polls on one eventfd takes 17.06s, 0.02s with this change. With voluntary preemption the soft lockup watchdog fires: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 26s! [repro:100] RIP: 0010:io_cancel_req_match+0x19/0xa0 io_poll_cancel+0x73/0x170 io_try_cancel+0x7b/0xf0 __io_async_cancel+0x41/0x110 Walk the hash once and cancel every match, as io_cancel_remove() does for futex and waitid. Cancel by user_data only needs its own bucket. __io_async_cancel() still loops until nothing is found, so a request that io-wq parks in the poll hash meanwhile is still cancelled. A cancel that matches one request now walks the whole hash twice instead of stopping at the match.

t: D-Link DIR-600L fatlady hedwig.cgi path traversal
d: A weakness has been identified in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file hedwig.cgi of the component fatlady Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to path traversal. The attack may be launched remotely.

A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the web management service of the Ethernet Remote I/Os products. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient bounds checking of specially crafted HTTP requests, potentially causing the web management service to crash and resulting in a denial-of-service condition.

t: Github.com/kuadrant/kuadrant-operator: github.com/kuadrant/wasm-shim: kuadrant-operator: authpolicy is silently bypassed (fail-open) when a tokenratelimitpolicy
d: A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. When a TokenRateLimitPolicy is attached to an HTTPRoute that also has an AuthPolicy - or when a RateLimitPolicy with defaults or overrides is attached to the Gateway or listener of such routes - the shim's action pipeline fails to dispatch the authentication guard at request time, and the request is forwarded upstream. Unauthenticated requests return 200 OK instead of 401, and neither authentication nor rate limiting is enforced. Both policies continue to report Enforced, leaving no status-level indication of the failure.

A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the SNMP service of the Ethernet Remote I/Os products. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit improper handling of specially crafted SNMP requests, potentially leading to a denial-of-service condition on the affected device.

t: D-Link DIR-600L GENA gena.cgi genacgi_main os command injection
d: A vulnerability was identified in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected is the function genacgi_main of the file gena.cgi of the component GENA Handler. Such manipulation leads to os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

t: TRENDnet TEW-657BRM mini_httpd entries information disclosure
d: A vulnerability has been found in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /usr/www/images/.svn/entries of the component mini_httpd. The manipulation leads to information disclosure. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor explains: "I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

t: Konstanty libmodplug ABC File load_abc.cpp abc_add_drum out-of-bounds
d: A flaw has been found in Konstanty libmodplug up to 0.8.9.1. The affected element is the function abc_add_drum of the file src/load_abc.cpp of the component ABC File Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading to version 0.8.9.2 is sufficient to fix this issue. This patch is called 540f0b8ec3d7979e17a8d6a55e31b8a7b734d463. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

t: declare-lab tango Model Loading tango.py Tango.__init__ input validation
d: A vulnerability was detected in declare-lab tango up to 34ecd38898508017ca937508a047b42817d2b070. Impacted is the function Tango.__init__ of the file tango.py of the component Model Loading. Performing a manipulation of the argument scheduler_name results in improper input validation. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. This product adopts a rolling release strategy to maintain continuous delivery. Therefore, version details for affected or updated releases cannot be specified. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

t: Lightbox with PhotoSwipe < 5.19.0 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Comment Link URL in Share Menu
d: The Lightbox with PhotoSwipe WordPress plugin before 5.19.0 does not escape image link URLs before outputting them in the attributes of the lightbox share menu, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks via comments when the PhotoSwipe 4 frontend is used.

t: User Registration Aide <= 1.5.3.8 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Password Update Page
d: The User Registration Aide WordPress plugin through 1.5.3.8 does not verify the current password or a reset token before changing a user's password, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a user's username and email address to change the password of any account, including administrators, and take it over.

An improper firmware authenticity verification vulnerability exists in the affected Ethernet Switches products. An authenticated remote attacker with administrative privileges could exploit the lack of cryptographic signature verification to install unauthorized firmware, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the affected device.

t: cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by() get_supported_features() assigns entries->num_features only after the memcpy() loop that fills entries->ent[] has already run. Since ent[] is __counted_by(num_features), the compiler's bounds instrumentation sees a 0-length array during that loop and FORTIFY_SOURCE trips on the memcpy. Set @num_features right after allocation, before any write into ent[], so the bound is correct for the whole lifetime of the array. This was found via a fortify panic: memcpy: detected buffer overflow: 384 byte write of buffer size 0 WARNING: lib/string_helpers.c:1035 at __fortify_report+0x54/0xa0 kernel BUG at lib/string_helpers.c:1043! Call trace: __fortify_panic+0x10/0x18 get_supported_features.isra.0+0x4a0/0x4d0 [cxl_core] devm_cxl_setup_features+0x84/0x120 [cxl_core] cxl_pci_probe+0x254/0x5e0 [cxl_pci] Same class of bug, same fix shape as commit 6c9d2e87df40 ("cxl/fwctl: Fix __fortify_panic"), which fixed the analogous issue in cxlctl_get_supported_features() but missed this one. [ dj: Fixed up title typo per Jonathan. ]

t: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states A peer can send configuration messages while an incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the security or deferred accept gate has completed. A configuration response can then promote the channel to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also act on channels that are closing, and a late connection response can move a disconnecting channel back to BT_CONFIG. Accept connection responses only while waiting in BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete configuration in BT_CONFIG.

t: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then sends its connection request. A peer can answer it before that with a connection response matching our source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG, completes configuration and becomes connected before security has completed. If security then fails, l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach the required security level. A connection response with a zero source CID is matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the same identifier for a response it still has to send, so the lookup can pick the wrong channel. Only accept a connection response while our request is outstanding, and only look at such channels when matching by identifier.

t: smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect TREE_DISCONNECT closes the tree's published file handles before marking and removing the tree connection. A concurrent CREATE that already holds a tree reference can therefore publish its file after the close pass. When CREATE drops its reference, the tree can be freed while the published file still points to it. Mark and remove the tree connection before closing its files, and serialize both new-open and durable-reconnect volatile ID publication with that state transition. An opener is then either published in time for the close pass or rejected after disconnect with STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED. Keep a tree reference while a file carries its tree pointer. This protects asynchronous users that can defer the file's final destruction past tree disconnect. The close pass can race the successful FP_NEW to FP_INITED transition. Take the opening request's file reference atomically with that transition. This keeps the file alive until request completion even if teardown removes the ID immediately. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in proc_show_files (fs/smb/server/vfs_cache.c:126) Read of size 4 at addr ff11000101540f80 by task poc/153 Call Trace: proc_show_files (fs/smb/server/vfs_cache.c:126) seq_read_iter (fs/seq_file.c:231) proc_reg_read_iter (fs/proc/inode.c:299) vfs_read (fs/read_write.c:574) ksys_read (fs/read_write.c:716) do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84) entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121) Allocated by: ksmbd_tree_conn_connect (fs/smb/server/mgmt/tree_connect.c:35) smb2_tree_connect (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:2819) handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:368) Freed by: kfree (mm/slub.c:6801) handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:332)

t: xfs: improve dirent bounds checking in scrub and repair
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: improve dirent bounds checking in scrub and repair LOLLM complains that we don't do enough bounds checking of the directory entries in directory blocks when we're looking for errors or trying to salvage entries. Let's improve that with more detailed checks.

t: NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
