Before commit 1b1676180246 ("mm/gup: handle huge pud for follow_pud_mask()"), we performed that check in follow_devmap_pud() by testing for pud_devmap(). Let's fix it by just structuring follow_pud_mask() similar to follow_pmd_mask(), minus protnone stuff that does not apply and minus FOLL_SPLIT_PMD handling. That makes it much easier to spot any such inconsistencies. Perform the pud_bad() check early in follow_pmd_mask() and just forward the PUD value. We can drop the pud_present() check in follow_huge_pud(), just like we have in follow_huge_pmd(). Even though we are performing more changes than strictly necessary, the fix should be easy to backport.

t: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the page cache without checking whether they are uptodate. However, shmem fallocate() can leave newly allocated folios uncleared and not uptodate. Callers such as udmabuf can then expose uninitialized memory to userspace. Clear non-uptodate folios and mark them uptodate under the folio lock before returning them to the caller. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description and comment ]

t: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check. Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before starting the walk, just like GUP-slow. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

t: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated the length on 32bit. Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts from a 64-bit userspace length. Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with -EOVERFLOW early.

t: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pending missing faults before clearing the VMA's userfaultfd registration. With per-VMA fault locking, holding mmap_lock for write does not prevent another fault from queuing after the wakeup but before userfaultfd_clear_vma() write-locks the VMA. That waiter can then remain asleep indefinitely. Call vma_start_write() before waking waiters. Existing fault handlers queue themselves before dropping the VMA read lock, and new readers are excluded until mmap_write_unlock().

t: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger __tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger gets truncated, possibly to 0. On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a 16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So at least these two scenarios are affected. Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by properly using "unsigned long" for range_size. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

t: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a non-blocking invalidation, the interval invalidation started beforehand is left unfinished: the caller skips mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end(). Subsequent interval notifier operations can then wait forever. The only in-tree trigger is nouveau SVM, which uses both notifier types and rejects non-blocking invalidations. Reaping via the OOM reaper or process_mrelease() can therefore leave the GPU fault worker stuck, holding a reference that prevents the dying process's address space and memory from being freed. End the interval invalidation when an ordinary notifier fails a non-blocking invalidation, like mn_itree_invalidate() already does when an interval notifier fails. Make that handling clearer in the documentation of mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start_nonblock(). Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: simplify description, update function doc ]

t: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab() Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call mmu_interval_notifier_remove() when freeing a buffer object. __mmu_interval_notifier_insert() sets ->mm before validating the range, so a wrapping userptr range can leave ->mm set after insertion fails. Cleanup then tries to remove an unregistered notifier for which no mm reference was acquired. Set ->mm only after mmgrab(), once insertion can no longer fail. While we could fix radeon's code instead, setting ->mm on success only makes the code more robust. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

t: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped KSM folio. The folio remains in the stable tree and can gain new mappings without being dirtied again. Once marked lazyfree, reclaim can discard data that those mappings still need. KSM always marks a folio dirty when converting it to a KSM folio in try_to_merge_one_page(). Marking a folio lazyfree clears PG_swapbacked but leaves PG_dirty unchanged. Preserving PG_dirty makes reclaim restore PG_swapbacked instead of discarding the folio. This also protects folios that were already lazyfree when KSM converted them. Skip KSM folios before clearing their dirty flag, checking under the folio lock to serialize with KSM conversion.

t: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PFN mappings), __wp_page_copy_user() copies from the faulting user address. For remote faults, this accesses the wrong address space, resulting in wrong data getting copied. For example, user_events updates an enable bit in the registering process's memory. If that memory needs to be faulted in, user_event_enabler_fault_fixup() calls fixup_user_fault() from a work item. Placing the enable bit in a private PFN mapping can trigger this remote COW path. Reject these faults with VM_FAULT_SIGBUS when the target mm differs from current->mm: remote faults. Ordinary (non-PFN) mappings are not affected. The user-address copy dates back to commit 6aab341e0a28 ("mm: re-architect the VM_UNPAGED logic"); likely, actual ways to get remote faults in there on COW PFN mappings appeared afterwards. But the fix is simple and straight forward. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify comment and description ]

t: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bits shift bug") made holebegin and holelen unsigned before they are shifted, by casting them to pgoff_t. That is an unsigned long: on a 32-bit kernel the cast cuts off the upper half of the two loff_t values, so a hole which begins at 4 GiB or beyond is taken for one in the first 4 GiB of the file. truncate_pagecache() passes the new size of the file and asks for private COWed pages to be unmapped as well. If a file of 6 GiB is truncated to 5 GiB, everything from 1 GiB on is unmapped, and what a process has written to a private mapping of the range between 1 GiB and 5 GiB is lost: it reads the contents of the file again. Where the range has an end, the wrong range is unmapped instead of the right one. The page cache copes with that, as it unmaps every folio that it removes. The callers which only have unmap_mapping_range() to get rid of user mappings do not, for example drm_vma_node_unmap(), whose fake offsets reach beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit, and revoke_iomem() with physical addresses of more than 32 bits. Cast to u64 instead. Nothing changes for 64-bit kernels. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

t: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPABLE mappings. For user-mode faults, pending signals are processed before retrying the access. Kernel-mode faults on user buffers instead return directly to the faulting instruction. With persistent allocation failures (esp. memcg limits), a syscall, such as write(), can therefore loop while not dropping locks. Only suppress VM_FAULT_OOM when FAULT_FLAG_USER is set, allowing kernel-mode faults and GUP to fail and signal allocation errors. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

t: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mremap() on different VMAs in the same mm. Those VMAs can share page tables, so both operations can acquire the same pair of page-table locks. UFFDIO_MOVE orders the locks by address, while mremap() takes the source lock first. These conflicting orders can deadlock; mremap() holding mmap_lock for writing no longer helps. Move double_pt_lock() and double_pt_unlock() to mm/internal.h and use them for all page-table moves in mremap(). Preserve the source entry checks after acquiring both locks. Remove the comments claiming that exclusive mmap_lock makes lock ordering irrelevant. In move_ptes(), make sure to just recheck source and destination PMD after taking the locks and drop the overly-long comment. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: use new helpers consistently; simplify description and comments; move_ptes() fixup ]

t: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabling merge_across_nodes resets this count to 1, even if per-node roots were previously allocated. So when toggling "merge_across_nodes" 0 -> 1 -> 0, a scan that starts while the setting is 1 and continues after switching back to 0 can encounter stale unstable tree roots, resulting in UAF. Only root is allowed to change "merge_across_nodes", and the documented sequence is: "merge_across_nodes setting can be changed only when there are no ksm shared pages in the system: set run 2 to unmerge pages first, then to 1 after changing merge_across_nodes, to remerge according to the new setting." Let's fix it by tracking in ksm_nr_node_ids the actual number of allocated tree roots. remove_all_stable_nodes() and ksm_check_stable_tree() will now scan more tree roots (skipping the empty ones), which is harmless.

t: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can remain in the swap cache after the process that first mapped it exits. Its anon_vma can then be freed, so ksm_might_need_to_copy() must not dereference it to compare roots. Doing so can result in some false-positives, resulting in the reverse mapping missing the new folio mapping, preventing migration and reclaim. SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU allows individual anon_vma objects to be reused immediately after freeing. A stale pointer can then refer to another anon_vma whose root matches, even though the target VMA is not linked to that anon_vma. Move the anonymous rmap compatibility checks into folio_anon_rmap_compatible(). Keep the page-index check and compare the folio's anon_vma pointer against the VMA's own anon_vma and root first. If neither matches, bite the bullet and walk the VMA's anon_vma_chain. The VMA keeps these anon_vmas alive, and finding a match guarantees that reverse mapping can find the new mapping. Lorenzo Stoakes says in a private discussion: "This isn't quite equivalent to the existing check. Every anon_vma in an anon_vma_chain shares the same root, but if you split a VMA then fork both of them like this: VMA A / \ <split> VMA B VMA C \ / root <- anon_vma 1 ----^ ^---- <fork> / parent \ anon_vma 2 anon_vma 3 | | VMA D VMA E VMA's D and E both get their own new anon_vma's such that: VMA D: anon_vma 2 -> anon_vma 1 -> root VMA E: anon_vma 3 -> anon_vma 1 -> root And if you found a folio referencing anon_vma 2, the existing check: anon_vma->root == vma->anon-vma->root Would be true for VMA's B, C, D & E. However after your change it'd be true for VMA D only, as it's the only one with anon_vma 2 in its anon_vma_chain. Whether or not that could actually happen in practice... 🙂 I don't know. [...] after your change it'd be true for VMA D only, as it's the only one with anon_vma 2 in its anon_vma_chain. [...] I would [...] say that you are making the test stricter but more correct. " If this affects performance when KSM was never even involved, we could just track whether KSM ever merged anything and just skip these checks. There isn't really a lot we can do otherwise: for mapped folios we might be able to use folio_get_anon_vma(), but for unmapped folios there really is no easy way to see if the anon_vma is still valid. Document the (confusing) lifetime requirements of folio_anon_vma().

t: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap slots can be read back as part of a large folio in the swap cache. ksm_might_need_to_copy() skips large folios, so another process can map a page with an incompatible anon_vma or page index. Reverse mapping then cannot find the new mapping, preventing migration or reclaim. Apply the same compatibility checks to large folios as to small ones. Pass the page corresponding to the swap entry and copy only that page when necessary. In do_swap_page()'s copy path, decrement only that slot's swap count, because the source swap-cache folio can now be large. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

t: mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge A driver can use the ->may_split() hook to forbid a VMA boundary at certain addresses. A device-dax device is a character device that gives raw access to a range of memory through mmap(). device-dax refuses any address that is not a multiple of the device's alignment through vm_ops->may_split. vma_merge_existing_range() can move boundaries, but does not call vm_ops->may_split. If a range at the edge of a VMA gets the attributes of the adjacent VMA, the function moves only that range over to the neighbour: one VMA shrinks and the other grows. This is a partial merge, and vma_modify() tries it before any split. Take a device-dax VMA that lies next to another VMA of the same file. The user calls mprotect() on the one page of the first VMA that touches the second VMA, and asks for the protection that the second VMA already has. The result is a partial merge. It puts the boundary inside a 1 GiB mapping, which is a single leaf entry at the PUD level. As part of the merge, the kernel looks for a huge PMD to split at the new boundary. That code does not expect a PUD leaf: vma_merge_existing_range() commit_merge() vma_adjust_trans_huge() split_huge_pmd_address() mm_find_pmd() treats the PUD leaf as a pointer to a PMD table, so the "table" is the device memory that the leaf maps __split_huge_pmd() reads a PMD that the user wrote to the device memory folio_put() on the folio that this PMD names Bad. While the code must at some point be taught to split PUD entries as well, the issue here is that we move VMA boundaries such that they are incompatible with the driver. Fix this by calling ->may_split() on the address that a partial merge would move the boundary to, and by abandoning the merge if the driver refuses. vma_modify() then tries the split, which fails with -EINVAL. Factor out existing split handling into check_split() and reuse it. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: improve description; cleanup the code ]

t: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can use PUD leaves while allowing VMA splits at page granularity. However, vma_adjust_trans_huge() only handles PMDs. After faulting a writable PUD-sized VFIO BAR mapping, changing its first page to read-only with mprotect() makes the PMD walk treat the PUD leaf as a PMD table. Applying MADV_DONTFORK to the first PMD-sized chunk leaves the PUD spanning two VMAs: the PMD-aligned boundary skips splitting. Walk the page tables once at each adjusted boundary and split a huge PUD or PMD leaf as needed. Handle PUD leaves even when the boundary is PMD-aligned.

t: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without VM_ACCOUNT. This can happen for read-only or MAP_NORESERVE mappings created with MAP_GROWSDOWN. Unmapping these VMAs does not release the charge, leaking Committed_AS. Only check and charge growth for VM_ACCOUNT VMAs, matching mremap(). Unaccounted growth skips the overcommit check while remaining subject to the other stack-growth limits.

t: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the page might still have a reference from the device. put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new owner while the original holder still references it. A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists. Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the pages inside are still in use. Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak. While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and switch to pr_warn_ratelimited(). [ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

t: mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock When offlining a node's last memory empties its tier, clear_node_memory_tier() calls device_unregister() while holding memory_tier_lock. A concurrent sysfs read can hold a kernfs active reference and block in nodelist_show() on that mutex. device_unregister() then waits in kernfs_drain() for the read to finish and release its active reference, while the reader waits for the offlining task to release the mutex. Return the node's former tier from clear_node_memory_tier(), making the helper more similar to set_node_memory_tier(), which also returns a memory_tier pointer. Let the caller unlink an empty tier under memory_tier_lock before rebuilding demotion targets, then unregister its device after dropping the lock.

t: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file() collapse_file() can call page_cache_sync_readahead() while still holding source folios locked. If truncate holds mapping->invalidate_lock exclusively and waits for one of those folios, readahead waits for invalidate_lock and neither side can make progress. We need to release those folio locks before starting readahead. On a page cache miss, roll back first, populate the collapse range, and retry once. Doing readahead after rollback avoids an extra pass when all folios are already present. If another miss occurs on retry, give up rather than keep retrying while truncate or reclaim removes folios. Keep page_cache_sync_readahead() and wait for read I/O with filemap_lock_folio(), releasing each folio before moving to the next. The existing uptodate check during collapse still handles read errors. Shmem uses shmem_get_folio() for swapin and fallocated folios without taking mapping->invalidate_lock, so it is unaffected.

t: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the page cache without taking the folio lock. khugepaged or MADV_COLLAPSE can therefore replace a folio after checking its refcount while memfd_pin_folios() still pins the old folio. The caller then receives a folio which is no longer part of the memfd. For udmabuf and iommufd, this can cause data corruption: DMA accesses the detached folio rather than the live memfd contents. DMA reads can return stale data, while DMA writes update the detached copy and are lost from the live memfd. The detached folio remains pinned, so these accesses do not constitute a use-after-free or target another application's memory. For memfd live update, the stale contents can reappear in the memfd after handover. Lock the folio and recheck folio->mapping before pinning it, like other page cache users do. If the folio was removed, retry the folio lookup from the index that was removed.

t: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly trigger a kernel warning with their own overlay mounts. They do so by changing the casefold flag of the topmost layer's empty root, the top directory of that layer, after the layers are set and before the mount is created. The casefold flag of a directory makes name lookups in that directory case-insensitive. All layers of an overlay must agree on casefolding. ovl_mount_dir_check() reads the casefold flag of a layer root when fsconfig() sets that layer, and saves the result in ofs->casefold. The mount is created later, by another fsconfig() call with FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE. The casefold flag of an empty directory can be changed. The casefold flag of the overlay root must match ofs->casefold. ovl_get_root() copies the flag from the topmost layer root, as it is when the mount is created. On a mismatch, ovl_get_root() only does a WARN_ON(), and the mount continues. The check is not a WARN_ON_ONCE(), so each such mount warns again. An unprivileged user needs CONFIG_UNICODE, and a tmpfs mounted with the casefold option in their namespace. Reproduced by changing the casefold flag of the empty upper directory after the layers were set and before FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE, with tmpfs and ext4 layers, and as uid 1000 in a user namespace. Fix this by replacing the WARN_ON() with a check that fails the mount with -EINVAL.

t: ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory can make the directory, or the whole mount, unusable. Lookups of the directory, and lookups in it, then fail. From code inspection, the caller only needs to own the directory. The upper filesystem must support casefolding: ext4 or f2fs with the casefold feature, or tmpfs with the casefold option. chattr +F and -F set and clear FS_CASEFOLD_FL, the casefold flag of a directory. The flag enables casefolding (case-insensitive name lookup) for the directory. All directories of an overlay must match the casefold state that was recorded at mount time, and ovl_lookup_single() enforces this: - A lookup in a directory that does not match fails with -ESTALE. - A lookup of the directory itself fails with -EREMOTE. ovl_fileattr_set() copies the directory up, which creates it in the upper layer if it only existed in a lower layer. It then passes FS_CASEFOLD_FL on to the upper filesystem. The upper filesystem accepts the change if the upper directory is empty, regardless of what the merged directory contains. The merged directory is the one that the user sees, with the names from the upper and the lower directories. After the change the upper directory no longer matches the mount. If the directory is the root of the overlay, the whole mount is affected. The flag can also change without chattr +F or -F. chattr reads all flags of a directory, changes one and writes all of them back. For a directory that only exists in a lower layer, overlayfs reads the flags from the lower filesystem. xfs with the ascii-ci feature reports FS_CASEFOLD_FL on every inode, but never sets S_CASEFOLD, the inode flag that overlayfs compares with the mount. So its directories count as not casefolded. With a lower layer on such an xfs and an upper layer on ext4 with the casefold feature, chattr +A on a lower-only directory therefore sets FS_CASEFOLD_FL on the new, empty upper directory. Reproduced as root on tmpfs and on ext4 with chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory whose upper directory was empty. Afterwards lookups below it failed with ESTALE, and lookups of the directory itself failed with EREMOTE. The chattr +A case was seen once, on a kernel with an earlier form of this patch that still passed the caller's flag on: lookups of the directory failed with EREMOTE. Fix this by returning -EOPNOTSUPP if FS_IOC_SETFLAGS, the only call that can change the flag, asks for a casefold flag on a directory that does not agree with the casefold state of the mount. This also refuses the chattr +A case above. [amir: check the flag against the casefold state of the mount instead of reading back the flags]

t: ovl: fix whiteout creation in casefolded directories
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fix whiteout creation in casefolded directories unlink and rmdir fail with EINVAL on an overlay with casefolded (case-insensitive) layers, if the name exists in a lower layer. Casefolded layers need CONFIG_UNICODE. Root can mount such an overlay, and so can an unprivileged user in a user namespace, with tmpfs layers. Overlayfs does not change a lower layer. To remove a name that exists there, it hides the name with a marker file, a whiteout. It creates the whiteout in the work directory, a scratch directory on the upper filesystem, and renames it over the name in the upper directory: - ovl_whiteout() creates the whiteout with mknod, or as a hard link to an earlier whiteout. - ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout() then prepares the rename with start_renaming_two_dentries(), which returns -EINVAL if the source or the target dentry is unhashed, that is, not in the dentry hash table. With casefolded directories, both dentries can be unhashed: - The target. Lookup in a casefolded directory leaves a negative dentry unhashed, so the rename target is unhashed if the name does not exist in the upper directory. - The source, which is the new whiteout. tmpfs hashes a dentry when mknod or link makes it positive, but ext4 does not, so on ext4 the source is unhashed as well. The cleanup after the failure also refuses an unhashed dentry, so on ext4 the whiteout is left behind in the work directory. Reproduced with rm and rmdir on casefolded tmpfs and ext4 layers, also as uid 1000 in a user namespace. Fix this by creating the whiteout with ovl_create_temp(), which repeats the lookup if the new dentry is unhashed. Prepare the rename with start_renaming_dentry(), which looks up the target name with the directories locked. The caller looked the name up without a lock, so return -ESTALE if the name now refers to a different inode. [amir: pass the name used for lookup instead of taking a name snapshot]

t: net/sched: clamp skb->queue_mapping before indexing the tx queue
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: clamp skb->queue_mapping before indexing the tx queue This issue was caught by Sashiko (nipa). A producer-side path cap is already merged (ea4d4b5dddb5); this patch adds the matching consumer-side caps. The issue: The tx queue is picked and capped in netdev_core_pick_tx() before the __dev_xmit_skb() qdisc enqueue path. A tc BPF program running inside an egress qdisc (not clsact) can then change __sk_buff->queue_mapping; that store is never re-checked. bpf_convert_ctx_access() bounds it only by NO_QUEUE_MAPPING, not by the device's queue count. Two consumers read the stale value: - On dequeue, qdisc_restart() calls netdev_get_tx_queue(), which indexes dev->_tx[]. netdev_get_tx_queue() guards it with just a DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE, so sch_direct_xmit() takes the out-of-bounds txq->_xmit_lock and writes txq->xmit_lock_owner past the end of the allocation on non-lltx devices such as ifb. Drivers that index their rings from skb_get_queue_mapping() (ex: ifb) go out of range the same way. - On enqueue, taprio_enqueue() indexes q->qdiscs[] with the same value; the array is sized dev->num_tx_queues. A duplicating netem on a child qdisc clones the skb and re-enqueues the clone at the taprio root (qdisc_root_bh()) through a direct rootq->enqueue() call, so the value reaches taprio_enqueue() before any dequeue cap runs. The Fix: Cap the mapping at the consumers and write the capped value back, so the qdisc's _tx[] lookup, the taprio q->qdiscs[] lookup and any later driver read stay in range. On the dequeue side the cap folds into the dequeue path instead of a separate walk over the returned list: dequeue_skb() caps the head, and each bulk helper caps the element it appends. For a qdisc that is not TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE, netdev_cap_txqueue() logs a ratelimited notice and selects queue 0. A TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE qdisc is bound to a single tx queue: dequeue_skb() uses q->dev_queue for the frozen check, the BQL limit and the trace point, while qdisc_restart() transmits on the skb's queue. Capping an out-of-range mapping to queue 0 would therefore send a per-queue child's skb through a different queue than the one it was dequeued for. On mq, mqprio, taprio and htb offload children, a stopped queue 0 could then park the list in q->gso_skb, and the later wake would schedule queue 0's own child instead of this qdisc. Pin a TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE mapping to the qdisc's own queue to keep the documented invariant. The pin covers every mapping, not only an out-of-range one: an in-range mapping that a filter sets on one of those per-queue children is rewritten to the child's own queue, and this path does not call netdev_cap_txqueue(), so it logs no notice. On a single-queue device qdisc_create() sets TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE, so the one-queue trigger described below also takes this branch and is corrected without a notice. That also keeps a bulk list on one queue by construction: every element of a TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE qdisc, including a follower changed by a filter, is pinned to q->dev_queue before it is appended. The fast bulk helper therefore needs no head comparison and no skb_bad_txq requeue; the slow helper, used only by non-ONETXQUEUE qdiscs, still compares and requeues a mismatched follower, where a wake on any queue reschedules q. On the enqueue side taprio_enqueue() caps the mapping against real_num_tx_queues and writes it back before selecting q->qdiscs[queue], so a duplicating child cannot steer the clone out of the array. Conditions to recreate the bug: The dequeue path: load a SCHED_CLS or SCHED_ACT program that stores __sk_buff->queue_mapping (a tc BPF action is enough), attach it to a transmit qdisc (for example a matchall filter on a prio root), and send a packet. With a 1-queue device a store of 1 indexes one past dev->_tx[]. Under KASAN with panic_on_warn=1 the unfixed kernel faults with "BUG: KASAN: slab-out- ---truncated---

t: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a permission event on an overlay directory, ovl_dir_open_realfile() opens the real directory via dentry_open(), not backing_file_open(), so the lower open could still raise FS_OPEN_PERM and deadlock a listener that also marks the backing filesystem. Export dentry_open_nonotify() and call it from ovl_path_open_realfile() when the overlay user file must not generate events. Ordinary ovl_path_open() callers are unchanged.

t: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores skb_transport_offset(), or the inner offset, in the unsigned hdr_len. A header in front of skb->data gives a negative offset. For an offset a little below zero, pskb_may_pull() gets a small length and succeeds. Then a 64-bit kernel reads the TCP header far after the skb and can crash. Further below zero pskb_may_pull() fails. Commit 28a57fb2c5df ("net: iptunnel: fix stale transport header during tunnel decapsulation") fixed one source of such offsets. Other code that removes bytes from the front of a packet can leave the same stale header. Return SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO for a negative offset in the TCP branch. SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 and the other GSO types read no header and still get a wrong qdisc_pkt_len(). On a 64-bit kernel only packets that cause the read after the skb today get a new result. Then __dev_queue_xmit() drops them and returns -EINVAL, but sch_handle_ingress() ignores the result. Their content can be valid. Thus the code that leaves the header stale needs its own fix.

t: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length(), the total guest descriptor length. virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() instead adds hdr->len to rx_bytes and buf_used, and budgets each queued skb as SKB_TRUESIZE(0). The guest controls the descriptor length and hdr->len independently. A guest can therefore provide a 64 KiB descriptor while declaring a zero payload. The descriptor-sized skb remains queued, rx_bytes and buf_used remain unchanged, and only the fixed queue-entry budget limits retention. This is not a lifetime leak: the skb is freed when dequeued or at socket teardown. Repeating this across connections can nevertheless exhaust host memory. On Linux v7.2, 455 such descriptors retained 30,255,680 bytes for a 262,144-byte receive buffer; a full-payload control retained 265,984 bytes. Vhost previously read hdr->len and allocated pkt->buf from that value. The conversion from virtio_vsock_pkt to sk_buff instead allocated receive skbs from the descriptor length, introducing the allocation-accounting mismatch. Copy the header into a stack object and validate hdr->len before allocating the skb. Size the allocation as sizeof(hdr) + payload_len so descriptor capacity no longer determines queued memory. Check payload_len against len - sizeof(hdr) to avoid addition overflow on 32-bit hosts.

t: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child. MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs. [ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

t: drm/amdgpu: keep the CS user fence BO in GTT
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: keep the CS user fence BO in GTT The CS ioctl hands the GPU the GART address of the user fence BO, but since the BO keeps its own preferred and allowed domains, it no longer makes sure the BO is in GTT. A user fence in a VRAM BO, which only needs to be a page in size, gets its address from amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset(), which warns about non-contiguous VRAM. On navi31, a CS with a user fence in a 4K VRAM BO, or in one created with AMDGPU_GEM_CREATE_VM_ALWAYS_VALID: WARNING: amdgpu_object.c:1531 at amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset+0x86/0xb0 [amdgpu], CPU#11: cs_gem_checks/18393 RIP: 0010:amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset+0x86/0xb0 [amdgpu] Call Trace: <TASK> amdgpu_cs_parser_bos.isra.0+0x4eb/0x850 [amdgpu] amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0x97e/0x2510 [amdgpu] drm_ioctl_kernel+0xac/0x110 [drm] drm_ioctl+0x2c6/0x5b0 [drm] __x64_sys_ioctl+0xa0/0xf0 do_syscall_64+0xa3/0x4d0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e and BOs which can't be in GTT at all, like GWS or OA ones of a page in size, pass the checks as well. Only take BOs which can't be anywhere else than in GTT as user fence, which the CS then validates there along with its other BOs. While at it, detect userptrs with amdgpu_ttm_tt_is_userptr(); amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_usermm() returns NULL once the task which created the userptr is gone. v2: only take BOs which can only be in GTT instead of special casing the user fence BO in the validation, use amdgpu_ttm_tt_is_userptr() (Christian) (cherry picked from commit f16989def9561d04d0f2e77216f5319112d29bf1)

t: drm/amdkfd: use the queue's process info for the WPTR BO eviction fence
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdkfd: use the queue's process info for the WPTR BO eviction fence amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart() removes the eviction fence of bo->vm_bo->vm->process_info from the WPTR BO of a new queue. bo->vm_bo is the VM which opened the BO last, not necessarily the KFD process' VM, and a render node VM has no process info. On navi31, an unprivileged process which exports its WPTR BO with AMDKFD_IOC_EXPORT_DMABUF and imports it on a second render node fd oopses in AMDKFD_IOC_CREATE_QUEUE: BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000060 RIP: 0010:amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart+0x86/0x1a0 [amdgpu] init_user_queue.part.0+0x180/0x250 [amdgpu] pqm_create_queue+0x32d/0x730 [amdgpu] kfd_ioctl_create_queue+0x583/0x9f0 [amdgpu] Pass the process info of the queue instead. With the fix, the queue is created and destroyed normally. (cherry picked from commit 6b4157498a176bd1c6083f6bb5aaf8a257a2027e)

t: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page tables without first calling amdgpu_vm_ready(). When a process is SIGKILLed, its VM entities are stopped. Teardown of an imported dma-buf then tries to clear PTEs by submitting to one of those stopped entities. That eventually hangs the task. Commit aa5fc4362fac ("drm/amdgpu: fix task hang from failed job submission during process kill") added the stopped entity check in amdgpu_vm_ready() and used it in amdgpu_cs_vm_handling(). That did not cover a call in amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify(), what was already mentioned in: https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/amd-gfx/2025-October/133076.html Tested by SIGKILLing a GPU workload holding imported dma-bufs. Without the patch "Trying to push to a killed entity" errors are logged, then a task hangs. With the patch there are no hung tasks. This was tested on a 6.18 kernel. (cherry picked from commit bee5c9d7a34cb1b510ad3b4c18c30f9d38b0ab7d)

t: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs") into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated. The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the running queue. On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT (debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr: amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10 amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd) amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000 from client 10 Validate the BOs on the individual needs_update list like before. (cherry picked from commit eb0d94765d4be18d41e93ad09947dd9cc06ed31a)

t: drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih Port this change to navi10_ih.c: commit afbf7955ff01 ("drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts") Setting IH_RB_WPTR to 0 does not clear RB_OVERFLOW if RB_ENABLE is not set. Pulse WPTR_OVERFLOW_CLEAR after RB_ENABLE (and with WPTR_OVERFLOW_ENABLE) so overflow is cleared when interrupts are enabled. (cherry picked from commit 713fb4ab04f4d2af6120f8eb607c5673b2759b38)

t: drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins [WHY] dal_ddc_open() cleans up pins it acquires on later failures. If the data-pin open fails, this attempt acquired nothing. If opening the clock pin or configuring fails, dal_ddc_open() closes the pins it opened. An extra dal_ddc_close() is unnecessary and unsafe: GPIO_RESULT_ALREADY_OPENED can mean AUX owns the existing handles, and closing them here would disrupt AUX. [HOW] Remove the extra dal_ddc_close() from the failed-open path. (cherry picked from commit 175ae7772b68757b4932f34ff862923cab7abe21)

t: drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-write of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL over MMIO without keeping GFX powered, unlike gfx11. When GFX is in GFXOFF at that point the update doesn't stick, and with the SPM VMID programmed on submission again, the job of a process with a reserved VMID can still run with the SPM writing through VMID 0. On navi48, after a few other submissions and a VM fault on the same VM, a COPY_DATA of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL from such a job reads 0 although the update was called for it: $ amd_uapi_regression --run-subtest cs-secure-ib-compute,gem-mapping-info-high-va,gpuvm-fault-high-va,reserved-vmid-spm-vmid amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:40 vmid:7 pasid:185) amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA1 (0xe) RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL in the job: 0x00000000 With GFXOFF disallowed around the update it reads the reserved VMID 15. (cherry picked from commit 907aebc5578ae09fa5c0e2f0784201295837e60b)

t: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto [Why] resource_get_otg_master_for_stream() can return NULL if no OTG master pipe is found for a given stream. The current code dereferences this pointer without a NULL check. This may lead to a possible NULL pointer dereference. [How] Add an explicit NULL check and skip the stream if the OTG master is not found. This is similar to dcn60_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto(). Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE. (cherry picked from commit ffde3d74c1faeeb645b66d02d02fdae3e073941b)

t: drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases drm_sched_job_add_dependency() consumes its fence reference on success and failure. Do not release the fence again if drm_sched_job_add_dependency() fails. (cherry picked from commit e04f3dfb2071451633e6440a3911a9bb65df9144)

t: drm/amdgpu: Report MES ring wait timeouts.
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: Report MES ring wait timeouts. Return -ETIMEDOUT when the fence wait before submission expires instead of reporting success without submitting the packet. (cherry picked from commit 34341594a87b4a3f28be41e3e70a4787f02b3d9e)

t: drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points amdgpu_atif_query_backlight_caps() stores the firmware's number_of_points as data_points but copies only the 99 points that luminance_data[] holds. number_of_points is a u8, so a firmware table that claims more makes the custom curve code in amdgpu_dm index past the array, and dm_query_extended_brightness_caps() copy past the end of the data_points[] buffer it fills Clamp the count to ATIF_QBTC_MAX_DATA_POINTS and warn, since a table that claims more is a firmware bug (cherry picked from commit af8a1c2b7d3de4960e10f94e8ba2fc0ccd168072)

t: drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails import_obj_create() takes a reference on the dma-buf for the new kgd_mem, but the error path after validating the BO doesn't drop it. Since the validation reserves the BO interruptibly, an import failing with -ERESTARTSYS leaks the exported BO with its memory, and keeps the module in use. Importing a 64 MiB VRAM BO in a loop while getting SIGUSR1 every 20 us and another thread changes the BO's mappings: INFO: 171821 imports, VRAM used before 65 MiB, after 129 MiB modprobe: FATAL: Module amdgpu is in use. Drop the reference, and free the sync object and the mutex of the kgd_mem as well. With that VRAM usage returns to 65 MiB after the same test. (cherry picked from commit b4d1eca2729840148ff2ea957724ce764ca5a94e)

t: drm/amdgpu: unlock the VM and BO when attaching a KFD BO fails
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: unlock the VM and BO when attaching a KFD BO fails kfd_mem_attach() locks the page directory and the BO with a drm_exec transaction on its stack, but leaves through the unwind label without drm_exec_fini() when locking fails, e.g. when MAP_MEMORY_TO_GPU gets a signal while the page directory or the BO is busy. Reservations already acquired then remain locked with their ww_acquire_ctx pointing into the expired stack frame. With one thread doing GEM_VA map/unmap on the KFD VM and another one mapping KFD BOs while getting SIGUSR1 every 20 us: BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in __ww_mutex_lock.constprop.0+0x34f5/0x3da0 ww_mutex_lock_interruptible+0x2f/0x150 drm_exec_lock_obj+0x107/0x2d0 [drm_exec] kfd_mem_attach+0x4dd/0x1b60 [amdgpu] and the process ends up in D state. Finish the transaction before unwinding. (cherry picked from commit 7b885fa27e4b9fa5cbdc64e66fc35872aee296f5)

t: drm/amdgpu: don't walk the CS chunks when allocating them failed
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: don't walk the CS chunks when allocating them failed amdgpu_cs_pass1() sets p->nchunks before allocating p->chunks, and the allocation failure path skips resetting it. amdgpu_cs_parser_fini() then frees the kdata of nchunks chunks from a NULL array. On navi48 with the chunk array allocation failed through failslab: Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f] RIP: 0010:amdgpu_cs_parser_fini+0x35d/0x710 [amdgpu] amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0xcae/0x7a20 [amdgpu] drm_ioctl_kernel+0x180/0x320 [drm] Set nchunks once the array exists. (cherry picked from commit 0c828445757b86aaa3ed2638832d76f450022bdf)

t: drm/amdgpu: don't drop the gang dependency fence twice
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: don't drop the gang dependency fence twice drm_sched_job_add_dependency() drops the fence reference when it fails, but amdgpu_cs_submit() drops it again, so the scheduled fence of a gang member loses a reference it still needs. A GFX+COMPUTE gang waiting for another context, with the xarray node allocation for the leader's dependency failed through failslab: WARNING: drivers/dma-buf/dma-fence.c:589 at dma_fence_release+0x34d/0x730, CPU#1: amd_uapi_regres/2993 drm_sched_job_cleanup+0x2c2/0x340 [gpu_sched] amdgpu_job_free+0xcb/0x3e0 [amdgpu] amdgpu_cs_parser_fini+0x435/0x710 [amdgpu] amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0xcd2/0x7a60 [amdgpu] Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f] RIP: 0010:dma_fence_signal_timestamp_locked+0x1b8/0x610 (cherry picked from commit 5aa070a83c8378810b906cc8bfc650ce69822a7c)

t: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page The host side does not know how much valid data will be returned by the target so it will typically provide a buffer larger than the amount of valid data in the ANA log page. The memory allocation used by the target does not guarantee that prior kernel memory contents will not be returned past the end of the valid page data. Fix this to ensure that the SGL is zeroed before copying the data.

t: arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE character device with major:minor 1:1, so opening it uses the /dev/mem file operations. It maps one page from offset 0xfffffffffffff000 at user address zero. The next openat() with a NULL pathname triggers a synchronous external abort (SEA, ESR 0x96000010) in strncpy_from_user() via do_getname(), panicking the kernel. valid_mmap_phys_addr_range() checks the exclusive end by adding the mapping size to the starting address. For this offset, the sum wraps to zero and passes the PHYS_MASK test, allowing an out-of-range PFN to reach remap_pfn_range(). The inclusive-end overflow check in mmap_mem_prepare() does not catch it because the end is ULONG_MAX. Reject starting PFNs outside PHYS_MASK and compare the inclusive length against the remaining physical range without overflowing. This also allows mappings that end exactly at PHYS_MASK, which the old check incorrectly rejects. [catalin.marinas@arm.com: changed the check to look more like __access_ok()]

t: ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin A file opened by file handle on an overlay with nfs_export=on can show the stale lower data of a file that was copied up to the upper layer. While the file opened this way stays in the inode cache, a lookup of the copied up file by path fails with ESTALE for all users. The open can also succeed for a file that was removed, where it has to fail with ESTALE. This happens with a handle that has one byte changed. The handle comes from an NFS client, or from a process that calls open_by_handle_at() with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH in the initial user namespace. When a file in a lower layer is about to be modified, overlayfs first copies it to the upper layer (copy up). With nfs_export=on, each copy up also creates an entry in the index directory, a directory that overlayfs keeps for itself on the upper filesystem. The handle of an overlay file that comes from a lower layer wraps the handle of its lower inode. Overlayfs calls this lower inode the origin. The overlay handle stays valid after a copy up. To decode such a handle, ovl_lower_fh_to_d() first decodes the wrapped handle to the origin. If no overlay inode is cached for the origin, it looks in the index directory: - An index entry there leads to the upper file. - A whiteout, the marker that overlayfs uses for a removed file, means that the overlay file was removed. The name of an index entry is the handle that copy up encoded for the origin, as a hex string. ovl_lower_fh_to_d() builds the name for this lookup from the bytes that the caller passed in. But handles with different bytes can decode to the same inode: - Overlayfs ignores some flag bits of the handle. - A lower filesystem can accept a different fid type, extra bytes, or generation 0 for any generation. Such a handle decodes to the origin but misses the index entry or the whiteout. So the decode returns an overlay inode that has only the lower file. While that inode is cached, a path lookup of a copied up file fails with ESTALE, since the upper file that the lookup finds does not match the cached inode, which has none. Reproduced on tmpfs and on ext4 with open_by_handle_at(), after a copy up and a mount cycle. A handle in which one flag bit, the fid type, the length or the generation was changed read the old lower data, and path lookups returned ESTALE. Fix this by re-encoding the decoded origin and building the index name from that handle.

t: l2tp: only return sessions of the given tunnel in l2tp_session_get()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: l2tp: only return sessions of the given tunnel in l2tp_session_get() Commit 5f77c18ea556 ("l2tp: use IDR for all session lookups") made pppol2tp_connect() and the netlink session commands find sessions with l2tp_session_get(), passing the socket of the tunnel they name. L2TPv3 session IDs are unique per network namespace, except that sessions carried over UDP are only unique per UDP socket, the socket of their tunnel. However, l2tp_v3_session_get() only checks the socket when another session has the same session ID. Otherwise it returns the session, whichever tunnel it belongs to. As of now, a session command that names the wrong tunnel acts on a session of another tunnel, and a PPPoL2TP socket for a second L2TPv3 tunnel fails with EEXIST, because it finds session 0 of the first tunnel. The issue can be reproduced with: ip l2tp add tunnel tunnel_id 3 peer_tunnel_id 3 encap udp \ local 127.0.0.1 remote 127.0.0.1 udp_sport 5003 udp_dport 6003 ip l2tp add tunnel tunnel_id 4 peer_tunnel_id 4 encap udp \ local 127.0.0.1 remote 127.0.0.1 udp_sport 5004 udp_dport 6004 ip l2tp add session tunnel_id 3 session_id 7 peer_session_id 7 ip l2tp del session tunnel_id 4 session_id 7 ip l2tp show session Before that commit, the delete fails with "No such device", and session 7 of tunnel 3 is still listed. After that commit, the delete succeeds, and session 7 of tunnel 3 is gone. This patch will make l2tp_session_get() return NULL when the L2TPv3 session it finds does not belong to the given socket. The receive path calls l2tp_v3_session_get() directly and is not changed.

t: drm/nouveau/nvkm: clear use.enabled when subdev init fails
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/nouveau/nvkm: clear use.enabled when subdev init fails On Kepler boards without the video decode falcon firmware installed (msvld/mspdec/msppp), every other VA-API decode attempt binds to an engine with no ucode loaded. The submitted work never completes, which leads to a context switch timeout, a channel recovery that cannot reset the engine, and eviction waits on fences that never signal. The process ends up stuck in D state, or killed by SIGBUS when it touches a buffer evicted after the wait times out: msvld: unable to load firmware data msvld: init failed, -19 fifo: SCHED_ERROR 0a [CTXSW_TIMEOUT] vo[5444]: channel 14 killed! WARNING: drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/engine/fifo/runl.c:117 at nvkm_runl_rc+0x2a4/0x3b0 [nouveau] [TTM] Buffer eviction failed WARNING: drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_bo.c:1092 at nouveau_bo_move_ntfy.part.0+0x9b/0x100 [nouveau] Tracing nvkm_subdev_ref() and nvkm_subdev_init_() shows the pattern: a reference taken with enabled=0 runs nvkm_falcon_init(), which returns -ENODEV; the next reference sees enabled=1 and succeeds without running it. Clear use.enabled when init() fails, so that every later reference retries init and fails cleanly. The other readers of use.enabled are fini() handlers that use it to skip teardown, which they now also do after a failed init(). On a GK107 (Quadro K1100M) without video firmware, playing H.264 with mpv --hwdec=auto: without this patch the GPU channel is killed within a minute and mpv hangs; with it, VA-API decoder creation fails, mpv falls back to software decoding, and no faults are logged.

t: ALSA: cs46xx: Handle SCB creation failures before dereferencing
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: cs46xx: Handle SCB creation failures before dereferencing With CONFIG_PM_SLEEP enabled, cs46xx_dsp_create_scb() can return NULL if kmemdup() fails to allocate the SCB data saved for resume. cs46xx_dsp_scb_and_task_init() and _dsp_create_generic_scb() dereference the returned pointer without checking it, causing a NULL pointer dereference on allocation failure. Check both return values before accessing the SCB descriptors. Return -ENOMEM when creating the null SCB fails and propagate NULL from _dsp_create_generic_scb(). Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE static analysis tool.

t: ALSA: hda/tas2781: Only accept CRC-less V1 data if all entries are valid
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hda/tas2781: Only accept CRC-less V1 data if all entries are valid Commit 408249089c48 ("ALSA: hda/tas2781: Accept V1 calibration data without CRC") only checked the first device entry. On machines where the BIOS populates fewer entries than p->ndev, the remaining all-zero entries are applied and tas2781_cali_preproc() divides by zero on playback open. Accept CRC-less V1 data only if every expected entry is non-zero and self-consistent (R0 * 1/R0 close to 1.0), otherwise reject it as before.

t: ALSA: line6: Reject capture buffers smaller than two packets
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: line6: Reject capture buffers smaller than two packets line6_capture_copy() splits the copy into the ALSA ring buffer once at the buffer end and wraps pos_done once, which is only correct when one packet holds at most buffer_size frames. The packet size comes from the device's endpoint, and the per-device hw structs allow 64-byte periods with periods_min 1, so a packet can be larger than the whole buffer. audio_in_callback() logs an oversized packet and then copies it anyway. The packet size is known at probe time, so constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_BYTES in snd_line6_capture_open() to at least twice the larger of the two endpoints' packet sizes. Two rather than one, because pos_done advances by the packet and wraps once, so a buffer of exactly one packet leaves the position unchanged after every packet. hw_params then rejects a buffer that cannot hold two packets, and the single wrap is valid for every configuration that gets through. Keep a guard in line6_capture_copy() that drops an oversized packet with a ratelimited error, for the case that should no longer be reachable. Reproduced on 7.3-rc7 with a USB/IP device presenting the GuitarPort interface layout and 1024-byte packets into a 128-byte buffer: ALSA logged "invalid position: pos = 224, buffer size = 32" and the driver logged "driver bug: len" on every following packet. With this patch a 1024-byte buffer is refused at hw_params, and a 2048-byte buffer streams for 30 s with no report and with the position moving inside the buffer.

t: ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails The three controllers that use the EP4 input URB allocate it before checking the endpoint type and before registering the input device. On failure they jump to exit_free_idev, which clears cdev->input_dev but leaves cdev->ep4_in_urb set. The card teardown then calls snd_usb_caiaq_input_free(), which returns early because input_dev is NULL, so the URB is never freed. Release the URB before dropping the input device on the error path.

t: ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs usx2y_urb_capt_retire() wraps the ring buffer once per packet and usx2y_urb_play_prepare() once per URB of nr_of_packs() packets of up to 50 frames. Both assume that the data fits in the buffer, and the hw constraints only require about two 1 ms periods, so a packet larger than the buffer on capture, or a URB larger than the buffer on playback, violates that assumption. Constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE in snd_usx2y_pcm_open() to at least two URBs, 2 * nr_of_packs() * 50 frames, for both directions. The bound is in frames and derived from the driver's own packet limit, so it does not read the endpoint, whose altsetting is only selected in prepare. Two URBs rather than one, because the position advances by a URB on playback and only moves when a URB is less than the whole buffer. Keep a guard in usx2y_urb_capt_retire() that drops a packet larger than the buffer, for the case the constraint makes unreachable. With nrpacks above about 163 (S16_LE) or 109 (S24_3LE) the bound exceeds the 64 KiB buffer the substream preallocates (twice that with the preallocation raised to its 128 KiB maximum), so hw_params fails for those module settings. That is intended: the driver cannot be safe with a URB larger than half the largest buffer. Reproduced on 7.3-rc7 with a USB/IP device presenting the US-122 interface layout and 1024-byte packets into a 512-byte capture buffer: BUG: KASAN: out-of-bounds in i_usx2y_urb_complete+0x1285/0x1ac0 Read of size 18446744073709551104 at addr ffff88800e448800 by task vhci_rx/83 Tested on 7.3-rc7 with the same device, S16_LE at 44100 Hz, nrpacks 4, so the bound is 400 frames. A 128-frame capture buffer and a 200-frame playback buffer are refused at hw_params with EINVAL. A 400-frame buffer streams for 30 s in each direction with the position advancing inside the buffer and no KASAN report; the capture guard did not fire. The same 400-frame capture buffer with S24_3LE, which selects altsetting 2 in prepare, streams for 30 s with the same result.

t: ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy usx2y_urb_play_prepare() sums the packet lengths of a whole URB, copies that many frames with a single wrap, and sizes each playback packet from the capture packet's actual_length. Three things are unchecked: that the URB fits in the ring buffer, that a packet fits in the playback endpoint's maxpacksize, from which tmpbuf is allocated, and that actual_length is a whole number of frames. The ISO descriptors take the raw actual_length while transfer_buffer_length and the copies take count * stride, so a packet that is not a multiple of the stride makes the descriptors add up to more than the buffer, by up to stride - 1 bytes per packet. Return -EPIPE, as the existing packet-size check does, when the URB is larger than the buffer or a packet is larger than maxpacksize, and size each descriptor from whole frames, so the descriptors add up to transfer_buffer_length and each stays within maxpacksize. The buffer case is prevented by the previous patch and this is the guard for it; the other two depend only on the device. The first case is reachable on the unpatched driver with ordinary packets: on 7.3-rc7, a USB/IP device presenting the US-122 interface layout and sending 48-frame packets, with a 100-frame playback buffer (two 50-frame periods, inside the stock constraints), KASAN reports: BUG: KASAN: out-of-bounds in i_usx2y_urb_complete+0x79b/0x1ac0 Read of size 18446744073709551280 at addr ffff88800e6b02e0 by task vhci_rx/80 With both patches, the same device and a 200-frame playback buffer is refused at hw_params with EINVAL, and a 400-frame buffer plays for 30 s with the position advancing inside the buffer, no KASAN report and neither guard message. The maxpacksize check is not exercised: the emulated device reports the same wMaxPacketSize on both endpoints. The descriptor case is visible with capture packets of 195 bytes at stride 4 (48 frames and 3 bytes): without this change the four descriptors add up to 780 bytes for 768 bytes of data, and USB/IP's completion check refuses the URB ("total length of iso packets 780 not equal to actual length of buffer 768", -EPROTO), after which the driver stops the streams. With this patch every descriptor is 192 bytes, the descriptors add up to the data in every URB for 30 s, the position advances inside the buffer and KASAN reports nothing. The 48-frame playback run above is unchanged.

t: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that may extend i_size, but clears the flag after ext2_get_blocks(). When the write uses an existing mapped block, iomap can then use FUA and skip generic_write_sync(), even though ext2_dio_write_end_io() updates the inode size. An O_DSYNC write can therefore return without persisting the new size. For example, on a FUA-capable device, a 512-byte O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC write at offset 512 into a fsynced one-byte file returns successfully and extends the in-memory size to 1024, while an immediate read of the on-disk inode still shows size 1. An explicit fsync persists the new size. Move setting of IOMAP_F_DIRTY after the initialization.

t: net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data While bytes spliced off the RMB are still in a pipe, recvmsg() waits for the pipe to release them before it copies the data behind them. The path to that wait skips the timeout and signal checks, and smc_rx_wait() returns at once on RCV_SHUTDOWN. With a signal pending, after SHUT_RD, or once the peer closes or shuts down writing, recvmsg() spins on a CPU until the pipe is drained, and SIGKILL cannot stop it. MSG_DONTWAIT and an expired SO_RCVTIMEO wait there too instead of returning -EAGAIN. Check the timeout and signals before that wait, and end it when the pipe releases the data or the connection is killed, not on RCV_SHUTDOWN. A zero-length read returns 0 without waiting for the pipe; a non-blocking one returns -EAGAIN while poll() still reports the socket readable (splice() can still take those bytes). The wait sets SOCKWQ_ASYNC_WAITDATA like smc_rx_wait(), so a byte arriving behind the pipe raises no SIGIO on a reader already asleep for it, and a full barrier orders its wait queue entry before its read of splice_pending, so no wake is lost.

t: drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset flop_reset_data_ppu is only allocated on GPUs that need the PPU flop reset. However, etnaviv_unbind(..) frees it unconditionally, and etnaviv_cmdbuf_free(..) dereferences cmdbuf->suballoc before checking whether cmdbuf is NULL. As a result, unloading the driver on GPUs that do not need the PPU flop reset causes a NULL pointer dereference at address 0.

t: drm/etnaviv: Flush the tile status cache through both the PE and BLT
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Flush the tile status cache through both the PE and BLT Since commit f232d9ec029c ("drm/etnaviv: fix TS cache flushing on GPUs with BLT engine"), jobs on GPUs with a BLT engine use a BLT command to flush the tile status cache instead of TS_FLUSH_CACHE, which is broken on most of these GPUs. GC7000 r6008/r6009 and GC8200 r6401 are the other way around: TS_FLUSH_CACHE works, but the BLT command does not flush the cache. The vendor driver handles these GPUs using TS_FLUSH_CACHE, but the etnaviv kernel driver has no way to identify them. As a result, dirty tile status cache lines survive the end of a job. They are written back by the next cache flush, using the page table of the job issuing it. If that job belongs to another process, the write goes to the wrong address space. On GC7000 r6009 this causes MMU faults and GPU recoveries blamed on an innocent process. I see around 1100 per run of a multisample depth/stencil test running alongside two other GPU clients. Emit both flushes at the end of every job on GPUs with a BLT engine. Whichever does not work on a given GPU is a no-op. Since dirty lines are only written back once, this costs one additional state load per job.

t: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listener directly instead of going through mptcp_listen(). It consequently misses setting SOCK_RCU_FREE on the parent MPTCP socket. tcp_child_process() can invoke the listener's subflow_data_ready() callback without holding the MPTCP parent lock or a reference to the parent. An authenticated MP_JOIN racing with endpoint teardown can therefore access the parent after its last reference has been dropped. The ADD_ADDR error path can also close an already published listener. Set SOCK_RCU_FREE before __inet_listen_sk() publishes the TCP listener, matching mptcp_listen(). This protects the parent on every subsequent close path, including a failed endpoint addition.

t: udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table extent closest to the goal. It keeps that extent's type and length together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only if goal_elen then reaches zero. UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1 (allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way. For such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the block after the extent, which is in use. The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use block. Subtracting a block from 0x40000000 then borrows from the type bits, and the extent becomes type 0 with a length of 2^30 - blocksize: about a gigabyte of "free" space overlapping live metadata, the other table extents and whatever lies behind the partition. From then on blocks are handed out twice, or past the end of the partition. Extents that udf_table_free_blocks() adds are type 0, where the check works, so only tables written by mkudffs or by another implementation are affected. Nothing more than filling such a filesystem is needed: on a fresh 1 MiB "mkudffs --space=unalloctable" image, creating empty files until the partition is full writes file entries over the reserve volume descriptor sequence and the backup anchor, and df then reports a negative amount of used space. On syzbot's images the same double allocation is what the two reports below trip over. In the first, ftruncate() extends a new file with enough hole extents to need a chain of allocation extent descriptors; one AED is placed on another inode's file entry, and a later one is placed on the block of the AED currently being filled, which udf_setup_indirect_aext() zeroes, so __udf_add_aext() finds lengthAllocDescs out of step with its cursor. In the second, an AED is placed past the end of the device, sb_getblk() fails, and the error path of udf_do_extend_file() calls udf_truncate_extents() on an extent list that no longer covers i_size. Keep the type separately from the length, as udf_table_prealloc_blocks() already does.

t: udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded udf_table_new_block() hands out the first block of the extent closest to its goal and trusts that the extent covers at least one whole block inside the partition. Nothing checks that. A zero-length extent makes it return the block the extent points at, which need not be free, and the subtraction of one block then underflows the length into the type bits, turning the entry into a bogus continuation. An extent running past the end of the partition makes it return blocks behind the partition. Such tables are not only found on crafted images: until the previous commit, udf_table_new_block() itself left zero-length extents behind in tables written by mkudffs, and then converted them into extents running past the partition. Check every extent once when the table is loaded, and refuse read-write access if one is empty, is not a whole number of blocks, or does not lie inside the partition, in the same way as for other allocation information the kernel cannot use. Check first that the table is an Unallocated Space Entry at all: the walk starts at the offset of the allocation descriptors in one, and for a file entry that offset lies before the inode's in-memory copy of the descriptors. Treat a chain of allocation extent descriptors that leads back to itself the same way: the walk would otherwise return the same extents forever, and the mount would never finish. Let a fatal signal interrupt the walk and fail the mount. Refusing read-write access to an empty extent is deliberate. It shows that an old kernel took the last block but left the entry behind. If consumed again, the entry returns an in-use block and turns into a huge bogus extent. Refusing the table before that happens avoids this second allocation; the filesystem can still be mounted read-only. The check cannot detect every overlap that may already exist in a damaged table. This patch should be backported together with the previous one: that patch stops creating new empty extents, and this one rejects existing ones before they are consumed again.

t: udf: fix preallocation discarding before an empty allocation extent
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix preallocation discarding before an empty allocation extent udf_discard_prealloc() finds the last extent of a file by peeking at the next one with udf_next_aext() and stopping when that returns 0. The peek reads into eloc and elen, and the code then uses them as the last extent. But when udf_next_aext() returns 0 they hold no defined value: if the extent list ends in a continuation descriptor that leads to an empty allocation extent, they describe that continuation, i.e. the block of the empty allocation extent, one block long. The kernel creates such lists itself: when udf_delete_aext() removes the only descriptor of the last allocation extent in a list, it leaves that allocation extent empty and the continuation to it in place. If the last extent is a preallocation, udf_discard_prealloc() deletes it with udf_delete_aext(), which finds the following allocation extent empty, so it also removes the continuation and frees that allocation extent's block. udf_discard_prealloc() then frees eloc and elen: that block a second time, instead of the preallocated blocks. On a space bitmap the preallocated blocks leak and the free block count drifts. On an unallocated space table the second free adds a second free extent for the same block, which is later handed out twice: fsx as run by generic/091 and generic/263 ends up with two parts of its test file in one block and reads back bad data. Peek into separate variables, so that eloc and elen keep the last extent that udf_next_aext() returned with 1.

t: udf: don't use eloc after the end of the unallocated space table
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't use eloc after the end of the unallocated space table When udf_next_aext() returns 0, its eloc, elen and etype outputs hold no defined value.
